Theoretical calculations indicate that the introduction of heterometals lowered the band gap of Fe-oxo clusters, enhanced the nonlinear hyperpolarizability, and improved the third-order NLO performance. Furthermore, the metal-oxo cluster-based polymer liquid crystal device prepared by mixing Fe 6 NaOC clusters with nematic liquid crystals not only has high transmittance and electro-optical switch characteristics, but also has stronger optical limiting performance. This work not only develops new high-performance NLO metal-oxo cluster materials with geometric symmetry engineering, but also establishes metal-oxo cluster-based electro-optical smart devices for nonlinear optical limiting applications.

title: Knotting a polymer chain into a trefoil
Critical surface strain regime for active and durable Pt-based oxygen reduction catalysts
Beyond the activity-stability trade-off in propane dehydrogenation
An integrated experimental and machine learning-based optimization framework for energy-efficient MEA/[TBA][Br] solvent in shipboard CO2 capture
abstract: Shipboard CO 2 capture (SCC) systems using MEA/[TBA][Br] solvent lack experimental studies and efficient data-driven optimization frameworks that minimize regeneration energy while maintaining high CO 2 capture rates. This study conducts cyclic experiments and develops a deep neural network (DNN)-based framework to optimize operating conditions for shipboard-relevant carbon capture. In the first stage, 70 experimental samples are collected under varying [TBA][Br] concentration, desorber temperature, and liquid-to-gas (L/G) ratio to train a surrogate DNN model. This model is used to formulate an optimization problem, from which an optimal operating zone is identified. In the second stage, 28 additional experiments are performed within this operating zone, and the full 98-sample dataset is used to train a refined DNN model, featuring three hidden layers with hyperparameters tuned via grid search and evaluated using an 80−20 training-test split. Optimization using the refined DNN identifies the optimal condition at [TBA][Br] concentration of 2.96 wt%, a desorber temperature of 120 C, and an L/G ratio of 1.73 kg/kg, corresponding to more than 90% CO 2 capture and a regeneration energy of 2.94 GJ/t CO 2 . This optimal performance corresponds to an 11.40%–34.87% reduction in regeneration energy compared to baseline MEA in this study and MEA-based SCC systems from the literature. The refined DNN demonstrates strong predictive capability, achieving MAPE values of 1.27% (training) and 1.41% (test) for CO 2 capture rate, and 0.83% (training) and 1.04% (test) for regeneration energy. Sensitivity analysis highlights the influence of all three variables: [TBA][Br] addition reduces sensible and vaporization heat requirements, higher L/G ratios improve CO 2 capture rates, and elevated desorber temperatures simultaneously enhance CO 2 capture rates and lower regeneration energy. Moreover, ATR-FTIR analysis over 15 cycles confirms solvent chemical stability with no evidence of chemical degradation. This work demonstrates an effective machine learning-enabled optimization strategy for SCC with MEA/[TBA][Br] solvent and offers insights into developing energy-efficient SCC systems and a framework extendable to other CO 2 emission sources.

title: Interface-confined etching towards mesoporous two-dimensional MoO3−x for high-performance planar supercapacitors
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal oxides (2D TMOs) have drawn broad interest owing to their great potential for catalysis and energy storage applications, but suffered restacking and poor conductivity. Porous and conductive nanosheets are highly required, while suffering from inefficient synthesis. Here, we demonstrate interface-confined etching to synthesize mesoporous 2D metal oxides. Ultrathin porous MoO 3− x nanosheets are successfully synthesized with 2–3 nm thickness and abundant 3–5 nm diameter mesopores, ensuring high specific surface area and 10 9 -time improved conductivity when compared to the pristine sample. Consequently, 2D MoO 3− x delivers ultrahigh volumetric specific capacitance of 2003.2 F cm −3 and energy density of 94.1 Wh L −1 at high power density of 1120 W L −1 , demonstrating great promise for energy storage. This work provides a promising way to synthesize 2D materials for high-performance energy storage.

title: Catalytic enantioselective synthesis via axial chirality transfer of transient atropisomers
abstract: Atropisomers have attracted growing interest in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Nevertheless, transient atropisomeric intermediates are often overlooked in catalytic asymmetric synthesis, and the chirality transfer processes mediated by these species have thus not been systematically explored or thoroughly studied. The catalytic enantioselective synthesis via a transient axial chirality transfer strategy effectively overcomes the reliance of traditional methods on pre-synthesized chiral substrates. By virtue of the precise stereinduction by chiral catalysts to generate transient axial chirality relays, it enables the efficient conversion of racemic or prochiral precursors into chiral functional molecules. This review focuses on metal-catalyzed enantioselective reaction pathways for the transfer of transient atropisomer axial chirality to central chirality and/or axial chirality. Through a systematic overview of the latest advances, current challenges, and future perspectives, this review is intended to offer comprehensive guidance and fresh perspectives for researchers in related fields, and to foster the development and application of novel chirality transfer strategies in asymmetric catalysis.

title: Solid-state host-guest chemistry of pillararenes and their supramolecular confinement effects
abstract: In supramolecular chemistry, macrocycle-based host-guest chemistry is of central importance, as it enables the selective recognition and reversible binding of guest molecules within well-defined host cavities through noncovalent interactions. Traditional research has mainly focused on solution-phase host-guest systems. However, in recent years, solid-state host-guest chemistry has attracted increasing attention due to its distinct advantages in constructing solid-state functional materials. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in the solid-state host-guest chemistry of pillararenes, with a particular focus on the resulting supramolecular confinement effects. Pillararenes were a class of macrocyclic hosts featuring rigid, electron-rich cavities, tunable rim functionalities, and symmetrical architectures, which have emerged as versatile platforms for constructing solid-state host-guest systems. Depending on guest size and binding mode, pillararenes can form diverse solid-state assemblies, including 1:1 inclusion complexes, 2:1 nanocapsules, linear supramolecular polymers, exo-wall binding architectures, and variable-stoichiometry systems. The confinement of guest molecules within pillararene-based crystalline frameworks not only restricts their molecular motion and conformation but also dictates their spatial arrangement, thereby giving rise to emergent physicochemical properties. These obtained solid-state host-guest systems have been successfully exploited in a wide range of applications, including optical materials, selective adsorptive separation, and structural determination. Finally, the remaining challenges and future prospects are discussed to guide further development in this field. We hope that this review will inspire researchers to explore the full potential of macrocycle-based solid-state host-guest systems and stimulate the design of next-generation functional materials harnessing the unique supramolecular confinement effects from macrocycles.

title: Alkynyl copper(I) nanocluster-assembled crystals based on polyoxotungstates exhibit photothermal and nitrate reduction properties
abstract: The construction of Cu(I) nanoclusters based on polyoxometalates initially encounters significant obstacles, particularly with respect to achieving crystallization within complex reaction systems. The synthesis of novel nanoclusters with enhanced functional performance poses an even greater challenge. In this study, four polyoxotungstate (POT)-constructed Cu(I) nanocluster-based assembly crystals are reported. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses reveal that POT units preferentially coordinate on the periphery of the Cu(I) nanoclusters, promoting the formation of one-dimensional (1D) or two-dimensional (2D) architectures while preserving the structural integrity of the POT precursors. Notably, the 2D assemblies exhibit superior photothermal properties among the synthesized structures. Comprehensive experimental and theoretical investigations indicate that POTs exert a pronounced influence on the charge transfer processes within these assemblies. Moreover, the catalytic activities of the nanoclusters were systematically assessed in the context of the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Remarkably, the 1D alkynyl Cu(I) nanocluster assemblies derived from an antimony-containing POT precursor demonstrated a substantially enhanced ammonia yield and Faradaic efficiency (FE), achieving an NH 3 production rate of 0.82 mmol h −1 cm −2 and a maximum FE of 93.51% under optimal applied potentials. These findings collectively reveal that both the photothermal and electrocatalytic performances of W–Cu nanocluster-assembled crystals are closely correlated with their distinct crystal and electronic structures.

title: Electrochemically-driven microemulsion demulsification enables anion-derived interphases for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries
Printable fullerene electronic transport layer for high-throughput fabrication of efficient and stable large-area perovskite solar modules
abstract: We demonstrate a simple yet effective strategy of incorporating poly( N,N -dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) into the [6,6]-phenyl-C 61 -butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) electron transport layer to regulate film morphology and interfacial properties in inverted perovskite solar cells and perovskite-organic tandem solar cells (TSCs). PDMAEMA suppresses π-π stacking through charge-transfer interactions between its tertiary amine groups (–N(CH 3 ) 2 ) and the π -system of PCBM, while the introduced steric hindrance further prevents fullerene aggregation, and its polar groups (–COO–) enhance the film’s polarity, thereby improving the uniformity and densification of the PCBM film. Therefore, the efficiency of printing prepared rigid and flexible devices (0.04 cm 2 ) reached 26.50% and 25.29%. Moreover, the efficiency of rigid and flexible large-scale perovskite solar modules (PSMs) reached 20.81% and 19.74% (100 cm 2 ), respectively, with the flexible module certified at 19.02%, and demonstrated excellent operational stability (>90% retention after 1000 h MPP tracking). Furthermore, the champion perovskite-organic TSCs show an efficiency of 26.96% and can maintain 94% of their initial PCE after illumination for 1000 h. These findings highlight the great promise of this molecular regulation strategy for scalable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: A GSH-responsive stapled oncolytic peptide-STING agonist conjugate for tumor-selective immunotherapy
abstract: Immunotherapy critically relies on sufficient release and efficient presentation of tumor antigens; however, most solid tumors undergo largely non-immunogenic cell death and harbor functionally suppressed tumor-infiltrating dendritic cells (DCs). Herein, we report a stapled oncolytic peptide-STING agonist conjugate (StTLM) that integrates a Temporin-La-derived stapled peptide (TLa-9), a glutathione-cleavable linker, and the non-nucleotide STING agonist MSA-2 into a single tumor-activated immunotherapeutic. In the reductive tumor microenvironment, StTLM is tracelessly cleaved to release TLa-9 and MSA-2. Hydrocarbon stapling endows TLa-9 with enhanced α-helicity, protease resistance, and tumor-selective membranolytic activity, thereby inducing potent immunogenic cell death with abundant release of antigenic materials. The released MSA-2 activates the STING-TBK1-IRF3 axis in DCs, promotes their maturation and boosts proin-flammatory cytokine production, thereby efficiently channeling oncolysis-derived signals into antitumor immunity. In a melanoma model, StTLM inhibits primary tumor growth by 95.9% and lung metastasis by 93.5% with minimal systemic toxicity, outperforming the individual components. This work couples immunogenic oncolysis with local DC activation in a chemically defined single molecule and provides a platform for dual-functional single-molecule cancer immunotherapy.

title: Beyond catalyst design: molecular interface engineering to regulate transition state for oxygen reduction electrocatalysis
Multi-spiro molecular design enables aggregation-resistant thermally activated delayed fluorescence materials for high-performance blue OLEDs
Ultrathin two-dimensional peptide nanosheets for chiral biomolecular recognition
Carbonyl swapping unlocks saturated heterocycles from cyclic ketones
Pore-engineering of biomimetic artificial proton channels for ultrafast proton conductivity
abstract: Developing artificial materials that achieve efficient proton transport by mimicking the Grotthuss-type hopping mechanism through ordered water chains in biological systems is crucial for energy technologies. Here, a pore-engineering strategy is demonstrated that exploits the conformational flexibility of a single building-block pair to access three polymorphic ionic hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks with distinctly different pore geometries and water-chain order. Among them, iHOF-55 , featuring a linear ordered one-dimensional channel, contains a perfect biomimetic proton transport pathway constructed from sulfonate groups, protonated amidinium moieties, and ordered water chains within its pores. It exhibits an ultrahigh single-crystal proton conductivity of 0.203 S cm −1 at 90 °C and 98% relative humidity, with the conductivity along the channel direction being 1951 times higher than that perpendicular to it, demonstrating remarkable anisotropy. Distribution of relaxation time analysis and molecular dynamics simulations reveal a transition from a high-barrier Vehicle-type mechanism to a low-barrier Grotthuss-type mechanism as the pore morphology evolves from a sawtooth to a linear structure. The highest proton mobility (2.17 × 10 −7 m 2 V −1 s −1 ) and the lowest activation energy (0.24 eV) among the three are both achieved in iHOF-55 , confirming the decisive role of ordered nanoconfined water chains. Through a comparative study of the polymorphic materials, this work elucidates a systematic structure-property-mechanism relationship, providing a new paradigm for the rational design of biomimetic proton conductors.

title: Knot your average anion receptor: doubly entangled Solomon links for sulfate binding in water
Surface-confined synthetic DNA circuits for rapid combinatorial recognition of cancer cells
abstract: Precise combinatorial cell recognition is limited by the slow, diffusion-limited kinetics of DNA circuits in complex physiological environments. Here, we report a surface-confined synthetic DNA circuit that overcomes this limitation by anchoring programmable DNA logic modules onto liposome membranes. This spatial confinement reduces the reaction space from 3D to 2D, driving proximity-enhanced interactions that dramatically accelerate reaction kinetics. The circuit executes a sequential YES-AND logic operation triggered by specific cell-surface receptors, enabling stringent discrimination of target cells from off-target populations. Notably, the platform identifies rare target cancer cells (as low as 0.1% of the population) in clinical serum within 10 min, achieving over 82% sensitivity and 92% specificity. This membrane-anchored architecture provides a generalizable strategy to accelerate molecular computing for early cancer diagnosis and point-of-care applications.

title: Precise length control in graphene nanoribbons: synthetic strategies and property correlations
abstract: Graphene nanoribbons (GNRs), as quasi-one-dimensional graphene nanostructures, constitute a highly tunable platform for next-generation electronics and spintronics. A variety of precision GNRs with well-defined edge and backbone structures have been synthesized via bottom-up approaches, driving forward research into their applications in fields such as single-molecule devices and quantum information processing. However, achieving precise and uniform length control remains a significant challenge. This control is essential not only for tuning fundamental properties such as charge carrier mobility and device performance, but also for meeting key practical requirements such as device integration and operational stability. To address this, synthetic strategies including stepwise and chain-growth methods have been developed, enabling the controlled fabrication of GNRs with defined lengths and topologies and thus facilitating systematic property investigation. This review first provides a concise overview of bottom-up synthesis methods and representative GNR structures. Building on these advances, we focus on strategies for achieving length control that enable the fabrication of GNRs with defined lengths and narrow dispersity. We further discuss how such synthetic precision deepens the understanding of structure-property relationships, particularly the influence of length on optoelectronic and quantum transport behaviors. By integrating controlled synthesis with property exploration, these developments lay the groundwork for advancing GNRs toward practical nanotechnology applications.

title: Molecular encoding of catalytic architecture for enantioselective catalysis in mesoporous metal-organic frameworks
abstract: Precise stereochemical control in heterogeneous catalysts remains fundamentally constrained because catalytic sites typically emerge only after framework assembly, intrinsically coupling their spatial definition to pore architecture. This limitation is particularly severe in mesoporous metal-organic frame-works, where enlarged pores enhance accessibility but weaken stereochemical discrimination. Here, we report a reticular design strategy in which the complete catalytic site architecture is molecularly encoded within a building unit prior to framework formation. A bifunctional BINOL-derived phosphate-carboxylate ligand integrates Lewis acid functionality and a spatially defined chiral environment in a fixed geometric relationship. Assembly with Zn 2+ generates a mesoporous chiral framework with ∼23 Å channels while preserving structurally locked Zn-phosphate catalytic sites embedded within preorganized chiral pockets, as confirmed by single-crystal analysis. Catalytic and control studies suggest a direct correlation between encoded site geometry and enantioselectivity, demonstrating a general strategy for programming catalytic function in crystalline porous materials.

title: Advances in photocatalytic deracemization reactions
abstract: Direct deracemization of racemates presents an ideal access to acquire highly enantioenriched molecules. Research in photocatalytic deracemization, since its first demonstration in 2018, has been advancing steadily and witnessed explosive growth in 2025, becoming a more diverse and active field. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in photocatalytic deracemization by categorizing the catalytic systems employed, including organocatalysis, metal catalysis, biocatalysis, or cooperative strategies, with a focus on their evolution and mechanisms. The diversification of catalytic systems has advanced the understanding of photochemical stereocontrol and offered useful guidance for the development of novel catalysts and the optimization of reaction systems. Moreover, these advances have laid a solid foundation for the preparation of valuable chiral compounds, enabling their broader application in pharmaceutical development and materials science.

title: Engineered nucleic acid nanostructures: biomedical innovations in oral healthcare
abstract: The global burden of oral health issues is becoming increasingly severe, with approximately 3.5 billion people affected by various oral diseases. Common conditions such as dental caries, periodontitis, and oral cancer not only directly impair oral functions, including chewing and speech, but are also closely associated with systemic diseases such as cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, and respiratory infections, representing a major public health challenge that cannot be overlooked. Current conventional oral treatments exhibit significant limitations in terms of lesion targeting, local drug retention, and microbial drug resistance, falling short of meeting the demands of precision medicine and long-term health management. Against this backdrop, engineered nucleic acid nanomaterials offer a breakthrough tool for constructing a new generation of intelligent oral diagnosis and treatment platforms, leveraging their programmable self-assembly capability, molecular-level precision recognition, favorable biocompatibility, and environmental responsiveness. This review systematically elaborates on nucleic acid nanostructures—including DNA aptamers, DNA origami, tetrahedral framework nucleic acids, DNA polyhedra, and spherical nucleic acids—which enable precise design and functional integration at the molecular scale, demonstrating broad application potential in several key areas of oral medicine. They can guide the ordered regeneration of dental and periodontal tissues, achieve sensitive detection and efficient antibacterial action against pathogenic bacteria while modulating inflammatory microenvironments, integrate diagnostic and therapeutic functions in oral cancer management for early identification and targeted treatment, and bridge oral and systemic health by regulating oral microbiota and immune responses, thereby driving the transformation of oral medicine toward precision, minimally invasive, and regenerative approaches. Although challenges remain in large-scale preparation, long-term stability, and clinical translation pathways, the deep integration of these materials with cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence is propelling their development into a powerful platform technology for systemic health management—not only in oral health but also beyond—promising revolutionary prospects for the future prevention, treatment, and health promotion of oral diseases.

title: Anticoagulant aptamers: from bench discovery to reversible clinical applications
abstract: Thrombotic disorders remain a major global health burden, yet conventional small-molecule anticoagulants often lack safety and specific reversibility. Nucleic acid aptamers offer a precise targeting coagulation with the unique advantage of “built-in” reversibility via complementary antidotes. This review examines the landscape of anticoagulant aptamers, highlighting the shift from bench discovery to reversible clinical applications. We critically analyzed translational obstacles using the clinical termination of the REG1 system as a major example, as well as other representative clinical cases, to illustrate challenges regarding nuclease stability, immunogenicity and production cost. Finally, we discuss emerging engineering strategies, such as novel conjugation strategies and enzymatic cyclization, to overcome these barriers, paving the way for next-generation systems that combine potent anticoagulation with rapid, programmable control.

title: Nitrite-driven hydrochemical regulation for enhanced ruthenium separation in a pyridine-based sorbent framework
abstract: This study introduces a nitrite-driven hydrochemical regulation strategy to reconfigure the ligand environment of ruthenium (Ru), transforming it from heterogeneous species into a uniform and stable anionic complex, [Ru(NO)(NO 2 ) x (OH) 5−x ] 2− . This transformation significantly enhances the homogeneity and reactivity of Ru, enabling highly efficient separation from high-level liquid waste (HLLW) using a pyridine-based resin. Combined density functional theory (DFT) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) analyses identified the dominant complex as [Ru(NO)(NO 2 ) 2.2 (ONO) 1.8 (OH)] 2− . To counteract the inherent instability of the nitrite-nitric acid system, a silicon-based composite adsorbent (N3/SiO 2 ) was developed, providing protective barriers against deterioration. Under optimized conditions, the adsorbent achieved a maximum capacity of 69.20 mg/g at 298 K—a 65% improvement over conventional systems. Adsorption and desorption mechanisms were elucidated, and a reusable ion-exchange-complexation cycle was proposed. This work offers an innovative strategy for Ru separation in HLLW, with strong potential for industrial scale-up applications.

title: Graphene-encapsulated Cu catalyst for highly selective and stable electroreduction of nitric oxide to ammonia without separation
abstract: The renewable energy-driven electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR) is a win-win strategy for ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis and pollution management. Yet the frequently used supporting electrolyte is accompanied by a product separation issue, which is often overlooked. The operation of NORR under acidic conditions can realize the direct utilization of ammonium (NH + 4 ) fertilizers/salts without separation. However, severe metal corrosion and the competitive hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) pose important difficulties for the highly stable and selective conversion of NO to ammonia. In this work, a graphene-encapsulated Cu nanoparticle catalyst (defined as Cu@C NPs) is designed for stable NORR within a duration of 100 h. A high Faradaic efficiency (98.7%) and yield rate (1327.9 µg h −1 cm −2 ) of NH 3 are realized on Cu@C NPs at −0.1 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), which are far superior to those of carbon-supported Cu/C NPs and other reported performances. The introduction of strain and a hydrophobic interface by graphene encapsulation can increase NO adsorption at the three-phase interface and lengthen the Cu–H distance, which inhibits the HER and proton corrosion, leading to a promoted and stable NORR under acidic conditions.

title: Plasmonic nanogaps bridging optical tweezers and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Nanogap-induced surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) represents an advanced platform for ultrasensitive, non-destructive molecular detection. But the detection sensitivity and reproducibility are compromised because only 0.1%–1% of the target molecules can reach the Raman-enhanced hotspots within the nanogap. Optical tweezers (OT) can capture particles into the nanogaps to achieve stable amplification of SERS signals, thus expanding the utility of plasmonic nanogaps for SERS applications. However, the combined nanogap-induced SERS and optical tweezers approach remains fraught with challenges, particularly regarding the complexity of molecular trapping within the nanogaps by optical forces. In this review, we outline recent developments in the construction of plasmonic nanogaps for enhancing SERS detection and OT-based molecular manipulation. Building on an analysis of the fundamental physics of optical trapping, we highlight key strategies to boost the combined SERS and optical tweezers approach bridged by plasmonic nanogaps. Our focus encompasses mechanisms, structural configurations, and capture modalities, with particular emphasis on the construction of static and dynamic nanogaps and on plasmonic optical trapping methodologies. Finally, we discuss current challenges and prospects to stimulate further progress in this promising field.

title: Precise chirality transfer and amplification in copper-cystine assemblies for enantioselective catalysis
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in life processes, chiral drug design, and functional materials. However, the precise transfer of molecular chirality to macroscopic structures remains a formidable challenge, and the control of chiral material morphology as well as the elucidation of chirality transfer mechanisms are technically demanding. In this study, D/L-cystine was employed as a chiral inducer to construct four-lobed, quadruple-rotationally symmetric copper-cystine assemblies (Cu-CST) via a facile solvothermal approach. This strategy enables precise transfer and amplification of molecular chirality into microscale architectures, providing a new model for cross-scale chiral studies. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed that it is Cu 2+ that primarily coordinates with carboxylate O and amino N atoms and constitutes the electronic-structural basis for stable chirality transfer. The assemblies exhibited pronounced peroxidase-like activity and catalyzed the enantioselective oxidation of D/L-3,4-dihydroxy-phenylalanine (DOPA) with high efficiency and precise chiral recognition, with DFT clarifying the underlying enantioselective catalytic mechanism. This work deepens the understanding of chiral supramolecular evolution, expands the repertoire of chiral functional materials, and provides a solid foundation for addressing precise chirality transfer to macroscale and harnessing chiral effects in catalysis.

title: Photoredox C–H difluoroalkylation of glycine derivatives via alkene difunctionalization: modular synthesis of fluorinated acidic amino acids
abstract: A photoredox C–H difluoroalkylation of glycine derivatives via alkene difunctionalization is presented. This three-component strategy enables rapid and modular synthesis of unnatural fluorinated α -aminoadipic acids. The protocol features metal-free conditions, a broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and high atom economy. Gram-scale synthesis and facile derivatization further underscore its practical utility. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that radical addition of tertiary alkyl radicals to iminium ions is the most plausible reaction pathway.

title: Bis-tridentate Ir(III) emitters with complementary carbene cyclometalates targeted for efficient blue phosphorescence and hyperluminescence
abstract: Abstract Blue phosphors present a significant challenge in the development of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). In this contribution, we designed a new class of bis-tridentate Ir(III) phosphors featuring two complementary carbene cyclometalates. They possessed efficient blue emission with short radiative lifetimes in both the solution and thin film states, which enhances the full utilization of electrically generated triplet excitons. Particularly, one PhOLED device had given an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 16.2% at 10000 cd m −2 , showing only a ∼4% roll-off from its maximum EQE of 16.9% at 2155 cd m −2 . Moreover, a related hyper-OLED device achieved true-blue emission with chromaticity coordinates (CIE x,y ) of (0.128, 0.107) and demonstrated a max. EQE of 32.7% and outstanding EQEs of 29.3% and 21.8% at a luminance of 1000 and 10000 cd m −2 , respectively. These results represent a significant advancement in the development of both blue phosphorescence and hyperphosphorescence with potential for practical applications.

title: Magnetoelectric synergistic heterostructured metal-organic frameworks for low-frequency electromagnetic wave absorption
abstract: With the advancement of 5G technology, the design of low-frequency electromagnetic wave absorbing (EMWA) materials still lacks high-performance solutions. Theoretically, a rational heterostructure integrating both magnetic and electrical materials can significantly enhance EMW absorption performance through the interface polarization relaxation effect. However, achieving a balance between magnetic loss and dielectric loss in porous homogeneous heterostructures remains a significant challenge. In this work, a heterogeneous core-shell structured Ni 3 (HITP) 2 @CoFe 2 O 4 (NCFs) composite with electromagnetic coupling behavior was successfully constructed in situ via a simple solvothermal method, integrating the dual contributions of dielectric loss and magnetic loss. Based on the interface-induced pinning effect, N–Co and N–Fe bonds act as pinning centers, establishing stable interface coupling and defect-mediated multiple polarization relaxation between conductive and magnetic components, alongside multiple reflection/scattering mechanisms and an effectively extended EMW propagation path. The resulting NCFs materials achieve a minimum reflection loss of −53.4 dB at 4.8 GHz, outperforming most low-frequency EMWA materials to date. Furthermore, radar cross-section simulations visually confirm the effectiveness of NCFs as high-performance EMW absorbing materials under practical conditions. This work provides a novel strategy for the design of low-frequency EMWA materials.

title: Catalyst-free, microdroplet interfacial electric-field-induced radical strategy for waste plastic conversion to diacids
Self-adaptive supracluster assembly of Ti8 macrocycles towards diverse (poly)rotaxanes
abstract: Rotaxanes, as a class of mechanically interlocked molecules with unique stimulus-responsive behavior and topological features, show broad prospects in functional materials. Current rotaxane assembly primarily relies on flexible organic macrocycles, while metal wheel clusters with rich photoelectric functionalities are often hindered by their inherent rigidity. This limits adaptive conformational adjustments and poses a significant challenge in constructing related rotaxanes. In this study, we successfully developed a series of (poly)rotaxane systems based on an octanuclear titanium-oxo macrocycle (Ti 8 ) under solvothermal conditions. By precisely regulating Ti centers bridging mode, we achieved fine control over the geometric shape and charge distribution of the Ti 8 macrocycle, enabling it to efficiently encapsulate a wide range of guests from solvent molecules, purely organic axles, coordination axles, to polymer axles. Thereinto, Ti 8 polyrotaxane with encapsulated infinite polymer axle displays distinct thermo-responsive dynamic behavior, which can be directly observed through single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) transformation. Besides, it also shows a significant blue shift in fluorescence emission and a markedly extended luminescence lifetime. This work not only provides a general and editable platform for synthesizing metal wheel cluster-based rotaxanes, but also opens a new pathway for designing regulable luminescent materials.

title: Phthalocyanine-based metal-organic frameworks: from molecular design to functional devices
abstract: Phthalocyanine-based metal-organic frameworks (Pc-MOFs) are rapidly emerging as a distinctive subclass of coordination materials with unique optoelectronic features and structural versatility. Their extended π-conjugation, capacity for metalation, and stability under operational conditions make them attractive for applications where conventional MOFs have often shown limitations. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of Pc-MOF chemistry, with emphasis on their synthetic design, structural diversity, and functional integration. Then, we examine their most relevant applications across three main areas: (1) Sensing. Pc-MOFs have enabled chemiresistive, electrochemical, and photoelectrochemical devices with enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, and low detection limits. (2) Catalysis. Studies in CO 2 valorization and oxygen electrocatalysis demonstrate that Pc-MOFs can achieve competitive performance by exploiting their electronic structure and redox-active centers, although the scope of explored reactions remains relatively limited. (3) Energy storage. The use of Pc-MOFs in supercapacitors and batteries has revealed promising charge-storage capacities, high cycling stability, and mechanical flexibility, pointing to their suitability for next-generation electrochemical devices. While Pc-MOFs still represent an emerging field with relatively few examples compared to other functional MOFs, the available evidence underlines their vast potential. The combination of phthalocyanine linkers with reticular chemistry offers unprecedented opportunities for rational material design. We foresee that continued progress in synthetic diversification and integration strategies will unlock their applicability not only in sensing, catalysis, and energy, but also in broader areas such as biomedicine, environmental remediation, and optoelectronics, in the upcoming years.

title: Disordered interfacial hydrogen-bond networks enhance selective ethylene production under ampere-level CO2 electroreduction
abstract: Engineering the hydrogen-bond network is essential for enhancing multicarbon (C 2+ ) formation during electrochemical CO 2 reduction. However, rational regulation of the hydrogen-bond network by modifying the interfacial water microenvironment remains a great challenge. Here, we develop an atomically dispersed Gd doped Cu 2 O that could attract H 2 O molecules and weaken O–H bonding, thereby facilitating water dissociation and providing sustained *H. The as-prepared catalyst achieved a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 63.5% for C 2 H 4 at an industrial current density of −1000 mA cm −2 . In situ spectroscopies reveal a substantial increase in the proportion of free-H 2 O species and a more disordered interfacial hydrogen-bond network upon Gd doping, which could modulate the *H transfer kinetics and suppress the hydrogen evolution reaction. Theoretical calculations confirm that the atomically dispersed Gd can modulate the interfacial water microenvironment, strengthen *CO 2 adsorption and promote the asymmetric *CO–*CHO coupling. This work establishes atomic-level rare-earth doping as a powerful strategy that achieves selective C 2+ production by engineering the interfacial water microenvironment.

title: Progress in the interdisciplinary field of artificial intelligence and chemistry
abstract: This review systematically summarizes the developmental background, core applications, and recent research progress in the interdisciplinary field of artificial intelligence (AI) and chemistry. AI has revolutionized chemical research by shifting it from a hypothesis-driven to a data-driven paradigm, establishing a “prediction-validation” closed loop and an interpretable model-assisted decision-making system. Following a logical framework covering electronic structure calculation, material application, spectral characterization, chemical reactions, and mechanistic essence, this paper elaborates on the application pathways of AI in chemistry, focusing on key directions including metallic materials, lithium-ion battery materials, semiconductors, inorganic crystalline materials, and biomaterials. Significant breakthroughs have been achieved in spectral analysis, reaction design, and microscopic mechanism elucidation, which effectively facilitate cross-scale information transmission. Despite these advances, the field still faces prominent challenges, such as data barriers, data heterogeneity, insufficient mechanistic exploration, and a shortage of interdisciplinary talents. Future research will focus on the construction of open databases, algorithm optimization, and the in-depth integration of AI with computational simulation and experimental validation, and an integrated research paradigm driven by data, supported by computation, and verified by experiments will be established to accelerate the in-depth application of AI in chemistry, thereby providing innovative solutions to global challenges in energy, health, and the environment.

title: Highly crystalline poly(heptazine imide) with exposed active sites for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen production coupled with glycerol valorization
abstract: Coupling photocatalytic hydrogen evolution with organic alcohol oxidation offers an efficient strategy to enhance overall photocatalytic performance; however, most inorganic semiconductors lack chemically specific active sites to precisely regulate the adsorption and oxidation pathways of glycerol. Herein, we rationally engineer poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) photo-catalysts by tuning the polymerization degree and exposing active sites through precise control of the molten-salt melting point, thereby simultaneously modulating charge-carrier dynamics and glycerol activation. The optimized PHI exhibits efficient visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution with an apparent quantum yield of 46% at 420 nm, while selectively converting glycerol into the high-value C 3 product dihydroxyacetone and suppressing the formation of low-carbon byproducts. In situ infrared spectroscopy combined with radical trapping experiments reveals a hole-driven, dehydrogenation-dominated glycerol oxidation pathway, elucidating the origin of the enhanced activity and selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of polymerization and active-site regulation in carbon nitride materials and provides design principles for efficient photocatalytic hydrogen production coupled with selective biomass valorization.

title: Proton-transfer-inspired photoswitches: mechanisms and applications
abstract: Organic intelligent materials are functional systems composed of organic molecules, which can generate signals or functional responses to external stimuli. In recent years, these materials have attracted much attention due to their wide range of applications. Among them, proton-transfer-inspired photoswitches have recently emerged as a distinctive class of photoresponsive systems, offering access to a diversity of photophysical outputs and exceptional performance in single-molecule state and solid-state environments, yet they remain comparatively underexplored and insufficiently systematized. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of recent advances in proton-transfer-inspired photoswitches over the past five years and establish a unified classification by dividing these systems into two fundamental categories, Type I and Type II, according to the temporal sequence of proton-transfer events. Particular emphasis is placed on photochromic mechanisms, structure-property relationships, and the central role of proton transfer in governing photophysical behavior in these organic smart materials. We further critically evaluate emerging functional applications enabled by proton-transfer-inspired photoswitching and highlight their unique advantages over conventional isomerization-based systems. Finally, we discuss the key challenges, unresolved mechanistic questions, and future research directions that must be addressed to advance the development of high-performance proton-transfer photoswitches, with the aim of providing conceptual guidelines for the rational design of next-generation functional materials.

title: Structure-electrochemical properties engineering of MnNi-MOF cathodes toward high-performance alkaline batteries
abstract: Alkaline secondary batteries, known for their low cost, high safety, and environmental friendliness, have significant potential for large-scale energy storage applications in the future. Recently, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have garnered significant attention as cathode materials for alkaline batteries. Unlocking their full electrochemical potential necessitates precise manipulation of both metal nodes and organic linkers. Herein, we present a systematic engineering of the structure-electrochemical properties of a bimetallic MnNi-MOF cathode. Upon electrochemical activation, MnNi-MOF converts to Mn/Ni hydroxides with intercalated terephthalate ligands. These organic ligands act as pillars to expand the interlayer channels for OH − ion insertion, while these ligands are bonded together by π-π interactions, resulting in the stability of the enlarged interlayer spacing. Additionally, Mn doping reduces the deprotonation energy of the nickel active sites, unlocking the full electrochemical performance. Compared to Ni(OH) 2 and Ni-MOF, the synergistic effects of the ligand-pillared interlayer spacing and Mn doping endow MnNi-MOF with superior rate capability and cycling stability. Specifically, it delivers a specific capacity of 251 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 and retains 72% of its initial capacity after 1000 charge and discharge cycles. This research provides deep insights into the electrochemical transformation and energy storage mechanisms of MOFs, offering a theoretical foundation for fully exploiting their electrochemical potential. These findings pave the way for the practical application of MOF-based electrode materials.

title: Nanopore architecture engineering for tuning the kinetics and cycling performance of hard carbon anodes in sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Hard carbon (HC) attracts significant attention as an auspicious anode material for commercial sodium-ion batteries. However, the relationship between the pore architecture and the kinetics and cycling stability of sodium-ion storage of HC remains poorly understood. Based on the construction of HC anodes with distinct pore architectures through multi-dimensional structure regulation of the lignin precursors, we systematically investigated the correlation between the pore architecture and the kinetics and cycling stability of sodium-ion storage. HCs with smaller pore sizes and abundant pores exhibit lower formation energy of sodium clusters, faster charge transfer rates, and more abundant diffusion networks for sodium ions. These properties enable HC to exhibit fast sodium-ion storage kinetics, thereby demonstrating superior rate capability and sodium-ion storage capacity at low operation temperatures. During high-current cycling, the graphene nanodomains of HC, rich in sp 3 -hybridized carbon content and large pore size, are prone to being destroyed. This leads to increased disorder in the graphene layer structure and decreased pore volume, accelerating the decay of the plateau potential capacity of HC. Moreover, the disordered graphene layer structure hinders sodium ion diffusion between interlayers, thus lowering the formation potential of sodium clusters and increasing the risk of sodium dendrite formation.

title: Electrochemically driven in-situ conversion toward a multifunctional solid-electrolyte interphase on graphite anodes for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries
Photocatalytic selective oxidation of α,ω-diols to high-value hydroxyaldehydes
Spatially controlled abiotic synthesis in living cells photocatalyzed by genetically anchored organic dyes
Dynamic adaptable network-driven synchronous migration of liquid metal for sustainable electronics
abstract: Liquid-metal (LM) elastomer composites offer an attractive route to intrinsically deformable conductors for flexible electronics. However, they frequently suffer from unstable conductive pathways induced by cyclic deformation, and their chemically crosslinked matrices render them unrecyclable. Herein, we report a processable and closed-loop recyclable liquid metal-polymer composite (LMPC) based on covalent adaptable networks (CANs). A unique synergistic migration mechanism enables polymer chain sliding to drive synchronous LM droplet rearrangement, effectively suppressing aggregation. Specifically, reversible disulfide exchange and hydrogen bonding endow the LMPC with topological reconfigurability and thermoplastic processability, while the metal-ligand coordination between Ga 3+ and sulfur atoms robustly anchors the LM droplets. This design successfully reconciles bulk processability with electrical stability. Consequently, the LMPC supports complete recycling and the precise three-dimensional (3D) printing of customized flexible architectures, including triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and capacitive sensors. Ultimately, alongside these manufacturing and integration advantages, the LMPC delivers a high electrical conductivity (∼1068 S m −1 ), excellent self-healing capacity, robust electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness (66.1 dB), and efficient low-voltage Joule heating (50 °C at 3 V). This work establishes a general strategy for the design of stable, multifunctional, and sustainable flexible electronics.

title: Functional nucleic acid-based molecular monitoring and modulation at biological membrane interfaces
abstract: Biological membranes, encompassing the plasma membrane and diverse intracellular membrane compartments, constitute the structural basis for maintaining cellular homeostasis and vital cellular activities. Decoding molecular events at these interfaces is essential for elucidating fundamental biological processes, regulating cellular behavior, and facilitating therapeutic intervention. However, the high dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and compositional complexity of biological membranes pose significant challenges for precise molecular analysis and manipulation. Leveraging their programmability, molecular specificity, and biocompatibility, functional nucleic acids (FNAs) have emerged as powerful tools for probing and engineering biological membrane interfaces. In this review, we summarize recent advances in FNAs, with a particular focus on their applications for membrane-related monitoring and modulation. We also discuss current challenges and further prospects of FNAs in advancing the study of biological membrane interfaces and their role in precision medicine.

title: Micro-nano composite structures resembling water strider legs constructed from polyoxometalates for efficient solar-driven interfacial evaporation and crude oil recovery
abstract: Emerging solar photothermal technologies demonstrate significant potential for addressing global freshwater and energy shortages, as well as for treating offshore oil spills. However, simultaneously optimizing hydrophilic and hydrophobic sites at material interfaces to balance the specific functions of efficient water evaporation, anti-saline fouling, and resistance to oily contaminants is a significant challenge. Herein, inspired by the dual properties of “hydrophobic gliding and hydrophilic moisture retention” observed in water strider legs, the competitive assembly of hydrophilic polyoxometalates and hydrophobic oleic acid anions with polyaniline cations is selected for fabricating an innovative heteropoly blue-polyaniline-oleic acid shell-encapsulated melamine foam evaporator (3D MF@HPB-PAn x -OA). Under electrostatic repulsion, hydrophilic HPB and hydrophobic OA respectively bind to the inner and outer sides of PAn, forming a unique spatially segregated structure. Hydrophilic HPB enhances evaporation performance by serving as an in-situ photothermal evaporation site. The hydrophobic armor layer enhances surface self-cleaning properties and the ability to treat oily substances. By leveraging its unique structural design and excellent mechanical stability, MF@HPB-PAn 10 -OA accomplished zero-liquid-discharge seawater treatment at an evaporation rate of 3.70 kg m −2 h −1 and achieved a recovery rate as high as 3.11 × 10 4 kg m −3 h −1 in highly challenging crude oil treatment scenarios.

title: Interfacial solvation regulation via self-assembled monolayers for accelerated charge transfer in low-temperature lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Achieving stable low-temperature operation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is still challenging. Current strategies primarily focus on reducing bulk-phase melting points. However, as the temperature drops, the solvation structure tends to reorganize into a more rigid and ordered state, rendering these bulk-modulation strategies increasingly ineffective. Furthermore, the increased structural rigidity of Li + solvation structures raises the desolvation energy barrier at the interface, leading to solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) instability, consequently necessitating effective SEI repair under low temperatures. Herein, we report a molecular engineering strategy that employs 2-methylglutaronitrile (MGN) to construct a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) on the graphite anode. This SAM synergistically regulates both the interfacial solvation environment and the bulk electrolyte structure, and these effects collectively lower the interfacial Li + desolvation energy barrier from 9.52 to 6.65 eV and disrupt the long-range ordering of solvent molecules. As a result, the optimized electrolyte exhibits a depressed melting point of approximately −60 °C and remains unfrozen at −40 °C. The LiFePO 4 ∥graphite battery delivers a high capacity of 113 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C at −20 °C, with negligible capacity fade after 300 cycles, while conventional electrolytes freeze. This interfacial-solvation regulation strategy provides a novel molecular design paradigm for high-performance lithium-ion batteries operating in extreme cold environments.

title: Single-molecule multifunctional organocatalyst enables accelerated and controlled ring-opening polymerization of N-carboxyanhydrides via hydrogen-bonding catalysis
abstract: The development of robust, controlled and chemoselective ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of α -amino acid N -carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) for producing high-performance polypeptide materials remains an appealing yet challenging goal. Herein, we first present a hydrogen-bonding catalytic system for the unmodified primary amine-initiated ROP of NCAs in an open vessel by utilizing an alkylated ammonium phosphate as a single-molecule multifunctional, noncovalent catalyst. This new universal catalytic system exhibits excellent tolerance to atmospheric moisture, different primary amine initiators, as well as impurities in NCA, enabling the synthesis of polypeptides with predictable molecular weight, narrow dispersity, and diverse C-terminal functional groups amenable to late-stage functionalization. Experimental data and density functional theory (DFT) calculations altogether reveal that this organocatalyst operates multifunctionally by forming a catalyst–substrate ternary complex. This cooperative interaction markedly binds and activates both the NCA monomers and initiators, substantially lowering the activation energy barrier of the polymerization. Moreover, it strictly follows the polymerization pathways of normal amine mechanisms (NAM) and facilitates the subsequent spontaneous decarboxylation step via a proton-shuttle mechanism. This study not only provides a robust and efficient catalytic platform for polypeptide synthesis but also establishes a new design principle, offering a conceptual blueprint for developing cooperative catalytic systems inspired by enzymatic functions.

title: Framework-mediated transport-catalysis cooperativity: iodine-tailored ion pathways and atomic-level adsorption interfaces break kinetic barriers in Li-S batteries
abstract: The practical applications of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries continue to face significant challenges arising from sluggish Li ion (Li + ) transport, lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling and sluggish reaction kinetics. To address this dual limitation, we propose a synergistic strategy integrating ion-conductive frameworks with catalytic phase engineering through the rational design of AHF-3-3I. This three-dimensional azolate hybrid framework features iodine-functionalized conductive nanochannels that establish directional Li + transport pathways with enhanced ionic conductivity, while the in situ phase-converted (IPC) LiI catalytic phase creates atomic-level adsorption-catalysis interfaces. The integrated architecture enables dynamic replenishment of catalytic sites and chemical confinement of LiPSs during cycling. This ion-transport/catalytic-conversion synergistic system achieves remarkable electrochemical performance, delivering a high reversible capacity of 812.6 mAh g −1 at 1 C with a capacity decay rate of only 0.019% per cycle after 800 cycles. The fundamental insights into framework-mediated transport-catalysis cooperativity presented here establish new material design principles for advanced metal-sulfur battery systems.

title: Engineering highly dispersed Ruδ+-Ov-Ti interfacial sites for enhanced low-temperature reverse water-gas shift reaction
abstract: The reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction holds significant potential for alleviating global warming and recycling CO 2 into high-value products through the CO conversion platform, yet achieving high activity in low-temperature RWGS remains a major challenge due to competitive methanation. Herein, we demonstrate that the high density of Ru δ + -O v -Ti interfacial sites with sub-1 nm Ru nanoparticles (NPs) can be constructed by direct H 2 treatment of Ru/anatase-TiO 2 precursors. The resulting sites efficiently catalyze RWGS, achieving 22.3% CO 2 conversion with >99% CO selectivity at a low temperature of 300 °C, approaching equilibrium conversion with high stability. Under optimized conditions, Ru/TiO 2 -R delivers excellent activity with nearly 100% CO selectivity at this moderate temperature, outperforming most benchmark catalysts. In contrast, annealing Ru/anatase-TiO 2 precursors followed by H 2 treatment leads to the formation of typical encapsulated Ru@TiO x active sites, which reduces accessible Ru sites and degrades catalytic activity by at least sixfold. Mechanistic studies confirm that Ru δ + -O v -Ti interfacial sites strongly favor the formation of the key COOH* intermediate and subsequent CO generation, thus significantly boosting low-temperature RWGS efficiency.

title: Matteson-type reaction under Barbier conditions enabled synthesis of tertiary boronates and beyond
abstract: Herein, we report an efficient method for the synthesis of tertiary boronates via the reaction of tertiary α-haloboronates with alkyl halides. This transformation employs magnesium as the sole mediator, proceeding through the in-situ formation of Grignard reagents (R-Mg-Br species) under Barbier conditions, followed by a Matteson-type rearrangement. This in-situ strategy obviates the need for careful handling of preformed Grignard reagents, enabling the reaction to proceed under mild conditions with enhanced functional group tolerance. Beyond alkyl halides, a broad range of other electrophiles-including aryl halides, chlorosilanes, and chlorogermanes, and more-can also be effectively coupled. Consequently, our method facilitates the straightforward synthesis of tertiary boronates bearing quaternary carbon(sp 3 )–carbon(sp 3 ), carbon(sp 3 )–carbon(sp 2 ), carbon(sp 3 )–carbon(sp), carbon(sp 3 )–Si, and carbon(sp 3 )–Ge bonds, which have traditionally been difficult to access. Additionally, an unexpected “boronate transfer” event for the synthesis of tertiary 1,1-diborylalkanes was also reported.

title: Electronic modulation of Ru nanoclusters by adjacent Ni single atom sites enables efficient bifunctional hydrogen electrocatalysis
abstract: Regulating electronic structures via metal-support interactions is a core strategy to address the sluggish kinetics of alkaline hydrogen electrocatalysis. Herein, we propose an interfacial electron modulation mechanism by constructing a Ru/Ni-3DONMC synergistic catalyst with atomically dispersed Ni single atoms (SAs) and Ru nanoclusters (NCs) anchored on 3D ordered N-doped macroporous carbon (3DONMC). Combined experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the Ni SAs strengthen electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) to induce spontaneous interfacial electron transfer from Ru to the support, which downshifts the d-band center of Ru and optimizes Ru–H bond strength to enhance catalytic performance. Meanwhile, the intrinsic oxygen affinity of Ni SAs enables preferential adsorption of hydroxyl species (OH*), thereby alleviating competitive adsorption at Ru active sites and accelerating Volmer-step kinetics. Benefiting from this multi-level synergy, the Ru/Ni-3DONMC exhibits exceptional bifunctional activity toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR). Specifically, it delivers an HER mass activity of 23.54 A mg −1 Ru at 100 mV, which is 41.3 times that of commercial Pt/C, and an HOR limiting diffusion current density of 2.7 mA cm −2 with remarkable CO tolerance. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), the Ru/Ni-3DONMC-based device achieves 1 A cm −2 at a low cell voltage of 1.74 V and maintains stable operation for 300 h with a degradation rate of 0.267 mV h −1 . This study presents novel insights into the design of bifunctional catalysts for hydrogen-energy conversion, promoting the practical application of integrated hydrogen production-utilization systems.

title: Optimizing the coordination of non-noble metal catalysts for efficient acidic water electrolysis
Hierarchical helical assembly of chiral Pd(II) complexes enabling amplified circularly polarized luminescence and efficient spin filtering
abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials hold great promise for applications in advanced optical technologies, yet molecular solids with high intrinsic luminescent dissymmetric factors (∣ g lum ∣) remain extremely rare. Herein, we report a solution-processable strategy based on the hierarchical helical assembly of a pair of enantiomeric tridentate Pd(II) complexes ( D )- 1 and ( L )- 1 . Driven by the antiparallel dimerization via short Pd⋯Pd contacts, these complexes assemble into intertwined helical nanofibers, yielding homogeneous thin films with exceptional chiroptical activity. Although the dilute solutions are essentially CPL-inactive, the optimized films display mirror-image CPL signals with ∣ g lum ∣ of up to 0.7, ranking among the highest values reported for chiral molecular solids. Morphological and spectroscopic analyses reveal that this chiroptical amplification originates from their hierarchical helical architectures. Notably, the helical nanofibers of these palladium complexes exhibit a significant chirality-induced spin selectivity effect, achieving an average spin polarization ratio of ∼60% at room temperature. The concurrent realization of high ∣ g lum ∣ and efficient spin filtering demonstrates that the hierarchically assembled helical superstructures enable the simultaneous amplification of both chiroptical and spin-transport properties. This work presents a versatile design strategy for advanced chiral materials that integrate optoelectronic and spintronic functionalities through controlled supramolecular engineering.

title: Radical relay unlocks electrochemical foscarnet synthesis from CO2 and phosphite
Topological engineering of polynuclear lanthanide MOFs for boosting scintillation performance
abstract: Lanthanide-based metal-organic frameworks (Ln-MOFs) have become an ideal platform for developing high-performance scintillators due to their inorganic-organic hybrid nature, yet still suffer from the relatively weak X-ray absorption and low tolerance to moisture. Herein, we demonstrate a strategic approach to enhance the scintillation performances of polynuclear Ln-MOFs via topological engineering. By assembling hexanuclear Eu 6 and nonanuclear Eu 9 clusters with tetratopic carboxylate linker (tcpp), two Ln-MOFs, namely Eu 6 - tcpp and Eu 9 - tcpp , were afforded, featuring (4,8)-connected flu topology and (4,12)-connected shp topology, respectively. Due to its high-connectivity net, high density of Eu 3+ ions, and suitable energy-level modulation, Eu 9 - tcpp exhibits superior photoluminescence quantum yield and radioluminescence intensity with respect to Eu 6 - tcpp , achieving a light yield of 9261 photons MeV −1 and a low detection threshold of 167 nGy s −1 . Leveraging the abundant coordinatively unsaturated sites of the Eu 6 cluster, the radioluminescence intensity of Eu 6 - tcpp can be substantially boosted through the introduction of secondary linkers comprising heavy halogen atoms or large π-conjugated moieties. Among the Eu 6 - tcpp variants, Eu 6 - tcpp-ndc with zll topology displays the highest light yield of 9463 photons MeV −1 and a low detection threshold of 153 nGy s −1 , attributed to the increased framework rigidity and the resonance energy transfer from auxiliary linkers to tcpp. Both Eu 6 - tcpp-ndc and Eu 9 - tcpp can be fabricated into flexible films to perform high-resolution X-ray imaging. Remarkably, Eu 9 - tcpp -based film can clearly resolve the objects in a sealed tube under X-ray irradiation in an aqueous environment. Our work provides a promising design route for high-performance and environmentally robust Ln-MOF scintillators.

title: T-shaped unit induced ABC stacked covalent organic frameworks for near-infrared-light-driven CO2 reduction
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) light-driven photoreactions present key advantages, such as reduced side reactions, deeper penetration, and greater spectral abundance. However, rational design and precise regulation of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with efficient NIR light absorption for fuel or chemical production—particularly in the context of photocatalytic CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR)—have not yet been fully realized. In this work, we address this challenge through the strategic synthesis of T-shaped unit-induced ABC stacked COFs, ZnPor-PIT-Ni-COF (PIT = 4,4′,4″-(1 H -phenanthro[9,10-d]imidazole-2,5,10-triyl)tri (benzohydrazide)), extending the light absorption into the near-infrared region. Ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) diffuse reflectance spectra and theoretical calculations demonstrate the synergistic effect of a symmetrical T-shaped molecular architecture and symmetry breaking within ABC stacking of ZnPor-PIT-Ni-COF on the exceptional near-infrared light absorption capability of the framework. This, combined with the improved separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers and the more exposed metal-active sites due to the ABC stacking mode, endows ZnPor-PIT-Ni-COF with outstanding photocatalytic activity for CO 2 RR with 289 µmol g −1 h −1 CO production and 94% CO/H 2 selectivity under NIR irradiation ( λ ⩾ 780 nm), surpassing the performance of most reported NIR-responsive catalysts. Meanwhile, ZnPor-PIT-Ni-COF exhibits remarkable visible-light-driven CO 2 RR activity, achieving a CO evolution rate of 627 µmol g −1 h −1 . This work presents a new approach for constructing two-dimensional (2D) COFs that overcomes the limitations of NIR chemical transformations and expands the applicability of COF-based photocatalysis.

title: Host-guest modulation of full-color circularly polarized luminescence via chiral macrocyclic frameworks
Surface reduction-induced Ru–W alloy formation on WOx to boost alkaline HOR activity and CO tolerance
abstract: Given the sluggish kinetics and CO sensitivity of the alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), developing efficient Ru-based catalysts is crucial. Here, using reducible WO x as a support, we control W migration from the WO x substrate to Ru by tuning the reduction temperature, yielding a partially alloyed Ru–W/WO x heterostructure and a fully alloyed Ru–W. The Ru–W/WO x catalyst exhibits superior activity and CO tolerance, achieving a kinetic current density of 3.78 A mg −1 Ru at 50 mV vs. RHE, which is 12.2, 19.1, and 2.9 times higher than Ru–W, Ru/C, and Pt/C, respectively. Upon exposure to 1000 ppm CO, Ru–W/WO x retains 82% of its initial activity, whereas Ru–W is completely deactivated. Mechanistic studies reveal that WO x not only modulates the electronic structure of Ru sites, but also strongly interacts with water molecules, optimizing *H/*CO binding energies and enhancing the H-bonding network. This work offers a strategy to boost HOR performance by simultaneously tailoring electronic structure and interfacial microenvironment.

title: Boosting selective semi-hydrogenation of cinnamaldehyde via optimized hydrogen dissociation on Pt dual-atom sites
abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of cinnamaldehyde (CAL) to cinnamyl alcohol is of great significance for fine chemical synthesis, yet it remains challenging due to the competitive activation of C=C and C=O bonds, which often leads to uncontrolled selectivity. Conventional single-atom catalysts suffer from insufficient hydrogen supply, while nanoclusters tend to over-hydrogenate, both facing stability issues in prolonged use. To address this, we develop Pt dual-atom sites anchored on defective carbon nitride nanosheets via a scalable one-step impregnation-calcination method. Combined ex/in situ characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that the dimeric Pt sites lower the H 2 dissociation barrier to an optimal value, promoting efficient yet selective hydrogenation while inhibiting undesired side reactions. Moreover, the robust dual-anchoring structure ensures exceptional stability over repeated cycles with negligible leaching. The as-synthesized Pt 2 DACs feature a unique coordination environment stabilized by both Pt–Pt metallic bonding and pyridinic N ligands, which confers an appropriate hydrogen dissociation capability intermediate between single atoms and clusters. This tailored hydrogen landscape enables outstanding catalytic performance, achieving high conversion and chemoselectivity simultaneously under mild conditions. This work provides mechanistic guidance and a design principle for achieving precise control over hydrogenation degree and pathway selectivity, which holds promise for semi-hydrogenation of CAL and other demanding selective hydrogenation processes.

title: Intelligent DNA nanodevices for molecular decision-making in biomedicine
abstract: DNA nanotechnology has evolved from a platform for static nanostructure construction to one for dynamic functional system engineering. At the center of this evolution are intelligent DNA nanodevices that sense molecular or environmental inputs and perform programmed decision-making to generate defined functional outputs. Despite rapid progress, the field currently lacks a unified conceptual framework for comparing these systems across different levels of information-processing complexity, from basic stimulus responsiveness to multi-input logic control and autonomous feedback regulation. This gap hinders a systematic understanding of how DNA nanodevices progress from single-input-triggered responses to multi-input information integration and, ultimately, to closed-loop autonomous behavior. Herein, we organize intelligent DNA nanodevices into three progressive levels: single-input-responsive systems, multi-input logic-gated systems, and autonomous feedback-regulated systems. This framework clarifies the transition from stimulus-triggered conformational switching to logic-enabled molecular decision-making, and ultimately to feedback-controlled network behavior. We further discuss the major translational challenges facing the field, including in vivo kinetic robustness, spatiotemporal programmability, and system integration. Finally, we outline how overcoming these barriers may guide the rational design of next-generation DNA nanodevices that integrate responsiveness, molecular decision-making, and autonomous regulation.

title: Recent advances in interfacial characterization and regulation of alkali metal anodes
abstract: Alkali metal anodes exhibit exceptionally high theoretical specific capacities and ultralow electrochemical potentials, making them among the most promising candidates for next-generation high-energy-density rechargeable batteries. However, during practical operation, these anodes encounter critical challenges, including the formation of unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, uncontrolled dendritic metal growth, and significant electrode volume expansion. These issues severely compromise both cycling stability and safety. These failure mechanisms originate from, and are governed by, the interfacial structure and physicochemical properties of alkali metal anodes. Therefore, precise interfacial regulation is essential for maintaining structural stability and improving overall electrochemical performance. Unlike conventional two-dimensional electrode/electrolyte interfaces, the interface of an alkali metal anode, strongly influenced by the SEI, should be understood as encompassing both a geometrical interface and a three-dimensional interphase composed of the substrate, the SEI, and the adjacent electrolyte. It is characterized by nanoscale thickness, compositional heterogeneity, spatial nonuniformity, and dynamic evolution. Despite its importance, the coupled physicochemical processes within this special interface remain insufficiently understood, and a systematic framework describing the individual roles and synergistic interactions among the substrate, SEI, and electrolyte is still lacking. In this context, this review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in alkali metal anodes, beginning with fundamental interfacial reaction principles and regulation mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on elucidating the evolution of interfacial structure, ion transport behavior, and metal deposition dynamics as influenced by SEI formation, substrate engineering, and electrolyte design. Furthermore, this review summarizes the applications of advanced characterization techniques, including electrochemical analysis, spectroscopic methods, and microscopic imaging, in probing alkali metal anode interfaces and interphases. Finally, future research directions are outlined, highlighting the need for integrating multiscale in situ and operando characterization approaches to achieve a deeper understanding of interfacial evolution and failure mechanisms under realistic operating conditions, thereby guiding the rational design and optimization of high-performance battery systems.

title: Balanced dual emission metal-sulfur cluster via ligand engineering for high-performance X-ray scintillation
abstract: Metal clusters, with their heavy-atom cores and chemically tunable organic ligands, hold great promise for X-ray scintillation. Unlike direct excitation, X-ray ionization yields a statistical 3:1 excess of triplet over singlet excitons; these long-lived triplets fundamentally limit scintillation efficiency via collision-induced quenching. Theoretically, a dual-emission mechanism, simultaneously providing radiative channels to both singlet and triplet excitons, offers an ideal solution by enabling dynamic and adaptive exciton allocation that suppresses quenching while accelerating radiation. Here, we demonstrate that ligand engineering with a donor-acceptor motif effectively tailors the excited-state composition of Ag 6 S 6 and Cu 6 S 6 clusters to achieve this goal. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the lowest excited states are dominated by radiative metal-to-ligand and intra-ligand charge transfer (MLCT/LCT) components. This configuration facilitates multichannel intersystem crossing and reverse intersystem crossing (ISC/RISC), enabling a balanced dual emission of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF, 56%) and phosphorescence (44%). The dynamic exciton allocation between these dual channels effectively mitigates singlet-triplet annihilation (STA) and triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA), leading to a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% for Ag 6 S 6 . Consequently, this cluster delivers an excellent X-ray light yield of 16659 photons MeV −1 and a low detection limit of 148.45 nGy s −1 . Furthermore, a flexible scintillator screen fabricated from this cluster achieves a record-high spatial resolution of 31.0 lp mm −1 . This work establishes excited-state composition engineering via rational ligand design as a generalizable principle for developing high-performance cluster scintillators by harnessing efficient dual emission.

title: Biselenophene imide-based acceptor-acceptor n-type polymers: structure-property-performance correlations and applications in organic electronics
abstract: Acceptor-acceptor (A-A) strategy is highly desirable for developing n -type polymer semiconductors by mitigating intramolecular charge transfer character and enabling deep-lying frontier molecular orbital (FMO) energy levels. Herein, we report a series of structurally diverse A-A polymers based on a biselenophene imide unit, with systematic backbone modulations via selenium substitution, π-conjugation extension, and cyano functionalization. It was found that cyano functionalization most effectively lowers FMO energy levels but simultaneously introduces steric hindrance that disrupts molecular packing, thereby compromising device performance. Furthermore, while π-conjugation extension improves packing ordering and film crystallinity, it sharply increases the content of face-on orientation, which is not optimal for efficient charge transport. In contrast, the all-selenium-substituted homopolymer poly(biselenophene imide) (PBSeI), despite its slightly higher FMO energy level (vs. cyanated analogues), exhibits a superior molecular ordering, tight π–π stacking, and high fraction of edge-on orientation, yielding excellent n -type performance with an electron mobility of 1.5 cm 2 V −1 s −1 in transistors and a thermoelectric power factor of 116.1 µW m −1 K −2 , both of which are among the highest reported values for A-A polymers. These results highlight the delicate interplay between electronic structure and morphology in governing device performance and provide key design guidelines for developing A-A n -type polymers for organic electronics.

title: Kinetically mismatched network dissociation and reconstruction enable high-strength post-activation bonding in dynamic crosslinked polyurethanes
abstract: Dynamic covalent crosslinked polymer networks offer attractive reprocessability, but their practical implementation is often limited by the requirement for continuous thermal activation during processing and solvent-assisted preparation. Here, we report a solvent-free scalable strategy for preparing dynamic crosslinked polyurethanes (CDAPUs) based on Diels-Alder chemistry by regulating the dispersion of powdery dynamic components in polyol media. The resulting materials exhibit strong adhesion to diverse substrates and maintain reliable bonding under harsh thermal conditions, achieving a maximum bonding strength of 17.17 MPa and nearly unchanged adhesion strength after ten bonding–debonding cycles. More importantly, we identify a dissociation–reconstruction window in the dynamic network and use it to enable post-activation processing and high-strength bonding, achieving an adhesion strength of 10.18 MPa, corresponding to over 90% retention relative to its high-temperature bonding. This work establishes a scalable and solvent-free manufacturing strategy for dynamic crosslinked polyurethane adhesives. It offers a practical route toward low-thermal-load assembly, repairable bonding, and sustainable adhesive technologies.

title: Cryogenic assembly of nucleic acids
abstract: Nucleic acid assembly has long been dominated by thermal annealing strategies. However, the emerging field of cryogenic assembly is expanding our understanding of how low-temperature environments regulate nucleic acid interactions and enable the formation of unconventional structures. In this review, we summarize recent advances in nucleic acid cryogenic assembly across three distinct states, i.e., cryogenic solution, frozen state, and freeze-thaw cycle. We emphasize the unified physical mechanisms underlying cryogenic assembly, involving thermodynamic effects, spatial confinement and concentration effects.
