Therein, morphological biomimetics is highlighted for promoting the access of artificial systems to an ecological niche compared to functional biomimetics. Many non-luminescent organisms have already been bionically mimicked in appearances and behaviors. However, existing morphological biomimetics of luminescent organisms still face significant limitations, as they often fail to simultaneously satisfy the three key criteria: stimuli-responsive fluorescence patterns, spatially heterogeneous fluorescence across different body regions, and the ability to perform complex locomotor behaviors. To address this issue, herein, a stimuli-responsive fluorescent hydrogel-based modular robot (SFHMR) was designed by combining stimuli-responsive fluorescent hydrogels and an adhesive hydrogel-based modular smart robot. The obtained SFHMR successfully completed morphological biomimetics of the luminescent organism Phrixothrix hirtus (PxRE) by changing fluorescence patterns when moved to corresponding circumstances. Therein, the quenching of fluorescent hydrogels G1 and G2, respectively, with switchable green and red aggregation-induced emission (AIE), was achieved by the destruction of AIE molecules F1 and F2 driven by imine bond hydrolysis upon trifluoroacetic acid. Besides, assembly of the SFHMR was achieved through adhesion of hydrogel G3, which originated from electrostatic interaction between cationic pillar[5]arene (CP5) and sulfonic acid groups on the interface.

title: Benzobisthiazole-based covalent triazine frameworks with extended π-conjugation and unique donor-acceptor configuration for efficient photocatalytic sulfide oxidation and thiophenol coupling
abstract: Photocatalytic aerobic oxidation using covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offers an environmentally benign and advanced route for chemical transformations, yet the development of photocatalysts that are both efficient and stable remains a substantial challenge. Here, we report the de novo design of an efficient COF-based photocatalyst by incorporating benzobisthiazole units into a conventional covalent triazine framework (CTF) to construct a highly extended π-conjugated structure and a donor-acceptor (D-A) configuration for photocatalytic sulfide oxidation and thiophenol coupling. Structural characterization confirms both the crystallinity and robustness of the resulting material. Property analyses reveal that it behaves as a photoelectric semiconductor, exhibiting high efficiency in photogenerated charge separation and migration. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements demonstrate that under light irradiation, BB-CTF generates singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) and superoxide radical anions (•O − 2 ), enabling remarkable photocatalytic activity in the oxidation of sulfides and the coupling of thiophenols. This work underscores that integrating benzobisthiazole into CTFs to create a new type of D-A architecture substantially enhances charge separation and migration, highlighting the promise of this molecular engineering for advancing photocatalytic oxidation.

title: Kinetic decoupling enables homogeneous phase evolution in single-crystal Ni-rich layered oxide synthesis
abstract: Multistep solid-state reactions in complex oxides often involve kinetically coupled transformations that generate spatially heterogeneous phase evolution. In Ni-rich layered oxides, dehydration of hydroxide precursors, lithium diffusion, and transition-metal oxidation occur within overlapping temperature windows, leading to uneven lithiation and structural disorder. Here we demonstrate that a rationally designed medium-temperature pre-sintering step kinetically decouples precursor dehydration from subsequent chemical lithiation. By tailoring precursor porosity and crystallinity, the reaction pathway is redirected toward homogeneous nucleation and spatially uniform growth of the layered phase, accompanied by a narrowed phase-coexistence window. In situ diffraction analysis reveals accelerated and synchronized phase propagation across the particle ensemble, suppressing reaction heterogeneity at its origin. This work establishes a general kinetic decoupling principle for programming solid-state reaction pathways in multicomponent oxide materials.

title: N-heterocyclic selenium radical-catalyzed [3+2] and [2σ+2π] cycloadditions to access carbocyclic nucleoside analogues
abstract: Selenium-centered radicals exhibit unique reactivity in covalent radical catalysis (CoRC); however, their broader application has been limited by poor structural tunability. Herein, we report a novel dicationic N -heterocyclic diselenide catalyst, (NHC-Se) 2 , that undergoes direct photoactivation upon purple-light irradiation to generate selenium-centered radicals without external photocatalysts. This platform enables efficient [3+2] cycloadditions of vinylcyclopropanes with vinyl-substituted purines, pyrimidines, and aryl alkynes, affording carbocyclic nucleoside analogues in up to 85% yield and with excellent diastereoselectivity ( dr > 20:1). The system also enables radical-catalyzed [2σ+2π] cycloadditions of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes, providing access to 1,3-disubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes as bioisosteres of meta-substituted benzenes. Mechanistic studies suggest that photoinduced Se–Se bond homolysis generates an N -heterocyclic selenium-centered radical that initiates ring opening of vinylcyclopropanes and promotes subsequent cyclization.

title: Electron-shuttle catalysis in organic transformations
abstract: Electron-shuttle catalysis has emerged as a powerful paradigm for regulating electron transfer in organic transformations, enabling selective generation of radical intermediates and precise control over reaction kinetics and selectivity. Recently, remarkable progress has been achieved in the field of metal electron-shuttle catalysis, leading to a mechanistic breakthrough beyond the classic C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) coupling paradigm and overcoming limitations associated with unstable alkyl-metal intermediates. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in electron shuttle-mediated organic reactions, spanning electrochemical synthesis, photoredox catalysis, and thermal-driven catalytic systems. Particular attention is devoted to the underlying mechanistic roles of electron shuttles in improving reaction efficiency and unlocking unconventional reactivity, which would further broaden their applicability in organic synthesis.

title: Correction to “Lung-targeted polyzwitterionic lipid nanoparticles for effective treatment of lung inflammation”
abstract: We regret that our article “Lung-targeted polyzwitterionic lipid nanoparticles for effective treatment of lung inflammation” (Sci. China Chem., 2025, 68: 1107–1116) contained an error. In Figure 2A, the image of the “Bioluminescence images of major organs excised from mice at 6 h post-injection” is incorrect. The corrected Figure 2 and corresponding figure legend are provided below. Nevertheless, this correction does not affect the results and conclusion of the paper.

title: The photo-transformable stabilizer leads to high-performance perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
Precise single-atom modification of lacunary germanotungstate-encapsulated silver clusters
abstract: Single-atom engineering in metal cluster cores enables precise control over material properties, offering definitive insights into structure-property relationships at the atomic scale. Herein, we present a pair of nanoclusters, {Ag} 5 (Ge 3 W 27 )} and {Ag} 5 Cl(Ge 3 W 27 )} , stabilized by a triangular {Ge} 3 W 27 } unit and sharing an identical {Ag} 5 } framework. The introduction of a single Cl atom in {Ag} 5 Cl(Ge 3 W 27 )} can induce divergent functional behaviors: enhancing photothermal conversion by reducing symmetry and modifying the electronic structure, while simultaneously impairing catalytic performance through active-site blocking. This work expands the structural library of polyoxometalate (POM)-encapsulated silver nanoclusters and reveals how a single-atom change can direct structure and function.

title: CO2 capture and utilization
Energy transfer-mediated organocopper catalysis enables borocyanation of unactivated alkenes via cyano group translocation
abstract: The excited-state organometallic catalysis via triplet-triplet energy transfer (EnT) has been recognized as a privileged strategy for enabling challenging or otherwise inaccessible elementary steps in ground-state transition metal catalysis. However, the potential of photosensitized organocopper catalysis remains unexplored, despite significant advances in ground-state copper catalysis. Herein, we report a copper/photosensitizer dual-catalyzed borocyanation of unactivated alkenes through a cyano (CN) group translocation pathway, affording diverse synthetically valuable β -Bpin substituted alkyl nitriles with high efficiency. A series of experimental studies combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the EnT from the excited-state photosensitizer to an alkylcuprate intermediate, facilitating the thermally disfavored nitrile insertion and the subsequent selective β -carbon elimination of the resulting excited-state azacopper intermediate, are crucial to the success of this transformation. This energy transfer-mediated synergistic method underscores the potential to overcome the inherent limitations in conventional ground-state copper catalysis.

title: Oxide promoters as architectural determinants of Cu-ZnO interfaces for steering CO2 hydrogenation selectivity
abstract: Multicomponent oxide catalysts such as Cu/ZnO/Al 2 O 3 are typical catalyst systems for industrial CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol, and their catalytic performance is highly dependent on the interfacial structures among the components. However, how different oxide interfaces regulate reaction pathways through their spatial arrangement and thereby determine product selectivity remains a critical scientific challenge. To address this, we employed a controlled synthesis strategy to construct two catalyst archetypes with opposite interfacial configurations: one, via Al 2 O 3 addition, forms a Cu-dominated interface consisting of large Cu particles decorated with highly dispersed amorphous ZnO species; the other, via ZrO 2 addition, forms a ZnO-dominated interface consisting of large ZnO crystallites hosting dispersed Cu species. Under identical reaction conditions, the two catalysts exhibit comparable activity but markedly different selectivity. Given that the Cu: Zn:Al/Zr molar ratio in both catalysts is 6:2.7:1 (with Cu being far more abundant than Zn), in the Cu-dominated interface, the highly dispersed amorphous ZnO generates abundant Cu-ZnO interfaces and oxygen vacancies, steering the reaction via the formate pathway and significantly promoting methanol formation. In contrast, in the ZnO-dominated interface, the large ZnO crystallites reduce the number of Cu-ZnO interfaces, redirecting the reaction toward the reverse water-gas shift pathway and yielding CO as the major product. Combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we reveal that the Cu-dominated interface facilitates rapid hydrogen transfer for methanol production, whereas the ZnO-dominated interface stabilizes kinetically inert intermediates, leading to pathway decoupling. These findings elucidate the essential role of oxide promoters as “architectural determinants” that control the spatial organization of Cu-ZnO interfaces, thereby governing the selectivity response.

title: Photoredox-catalyzed radical phosphinylation of [1.1.1]propellane via polarity match additions
abstract: Aromatic phosphinates represent privileged structural motifs widely employed in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. Despite their utility, synthetic access to phosphinated nonclassical arene bioisosteres, particularly those capable of improving key physicochemical properties of drug candidates, remains limited. Here we report a photoredox-catalyzed radical phosphinylation strategy for the synthesis of bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (BCP) phosphinates employing [1.1.1]propellane, arylphosphonites, and diverse electrophilic radical precursors. This novel BCP radical phosphinylation strategy features easy setup, mild conditions and broad scope. Electrophilic radicals derived from Katritzky salts, activated alkyl bromides, Togni’s reagent II, and disulfides perform additions onto [1.1.1]propellane to afford BCP radicals, which then engage in polarity-matched phosphinylation. This mechanistically distinct approach establishes a robust platform for constructing valuable BCP phosphinate bioisosteres, significantly expanding the toolbox for medicinal chemistry applications and enabling new opportunities in drug discovery programs.

title: Nuclease-resistant DNA polyaptamer hydrogels via supramolecular assembly: balancing molecular recognition and stability for targeted myocardial therapy
abstract: DNA polyaptamer-functionalized hydrogels offer a powerful chemical toolset for the recognition and manipulation of biological nanoparticles, such as exosomes (EXOs). However, their transition from in vitro tools to in vivo therapeutics is hindered by a fundamental trade-off: protecting the DNA scaffold from nuclease degradation often masks the aptamer’s molecular recognition interface. Herein, we report a supramolecular assembly strategy that resolves this conflict through stoichiometric control of DNA polyaptamers and poly- L -lysine (PLL) within a hydrogel matrix. By modulating the PLL/DNA ratio, we engineered a series of injectable hydrogels that tune the landscape between nuclease resistance and EXO-capture kinetics. While high PLL density extends in vivo retention from 2 to 11 days, it concurrently induces steric shielding that impairs polyvalent recognition. We identify a critical “sweet spot” at a PLL concentration of 80 µmol/L, achieving a synergistic balance of prolonged physiological stability (>6 days) and high-affinity capture of circulating CD63-positive EXOs. In a rat myocardial infarction model, this optimized supramolecular hydrogel enables the localized enrichment and sustained delivery of endogenous therapeutic EXOs. This spatiotemporal control achieves significant inhibition of fibrosis and enhanced angiogenesis, offering a versatile chemical platform for harnessing endogenous signaling agents in regenerative therapy.

title: Engineering a bacterial regulatory system for high-yield protein expression and in-cell 19F NMR in mammalian cells
abstract: High-yield production of functional proteins in mammalian cells is critical for structural biology and biologics development, yet efficient expression remains technically challenging with limited expression systems available. Here, we engineered the bacterial NarX/NarL two-component regulatory system into a robust gene-expression platform for mammalian cells, achieving strong induction of protein production in HEK293T cells. Through genetic optimization, this engineered system enables remarkably high expression levels of proteins typically refractory to conventional mammalian expression. We further demonstrate its application for in-cell NMR spectroscopy, which has long been constrained by insufficient protein yield in mammalian hosts. By incorporating fluorine-containing amino acids site-specifically, we obtained high-resolution in-cell 19 F NMR spectra, enabling direct monitoring of the conformations of target proteins and their interactions with ligands in cells. Collectively, this engineered mammalian expression system provides a versatile and transformative framework for cellular structural biology and holds significant promise for therapeutic protein production.

title: Interfacial electron bridging-driven switching from type-II to Z-scheme for selective valorization of lignin to vanillin by photocatalysis
abstract: The targeted cleavage of C β –O–4 bonds in lignin biomass is crucial for its depolymerization into useful chemical products. However, conventional thermocatalytic and harsh oxidative strategies often require energy-intensive conditions or suffer from poor product selectivity due to severe over-oxidation. To achieve mild and highly selective depolymerization, herein, we report an interfacial engineering strategy that drives the transition of Bi 2 MoO 6 /TiO 2 heterojunctions from type-II to Z-scheme by introducing an interfacial metallic mediator. Experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that Au considerably improves charge migration capability. This specifically triggers the formation of •C α radical intermediates, which dictate the targeted cleavage of C β –O–4 bonds. Compared to pristine Bi 2 MoO 6 and type-II Bi 2 MoO 6 /TiO 2 heterojunctions, the prepared Bi 2 MoO 6 /Au/TiO 2 Z-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst delivers a remarkable 99.8% conversion of the 2-phenoxy-1-phenylethanol (PP-ol) lignin model compound, yielding phenol and acetophenone at 95.3% and 93.2%, respectively. At a wavelength of 520 nm, the synthesized heterojunction attains a quantum yield of 0.053 for the efficient conversion of PP-ol, surpassing the most reported heterojunction photocatalysts. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform (DRIFT) reveals that Mo–O sites act as molecular “tweezers” to activate lignin biomass through phenolic hydroxyl coordination. This activation synergizes with the Au-bridged charge-transfer route, allowing efficient C β –O cleavage in alkali lignin extracted from Pinus massoniana under outdoor conditions, producing 45.5 mg g −1 h −1 of vanillin. By elegantly bridging interfacial charge kinetics with targeted substrate activation, this work provides a highly efficient and sustainable paradigm for precise bond cleavage in realistic biomass under practical conditions.

title: Dynamic monitoring of chemoresistant tumor cells enabled by an adaptive DNA nanoclassifier
abstract: Chemoresistance profiling is of considerable interest because it has proven to be a valuable technique for clinicians with real-time feedback for optimizing therapeutic regimens during treatment cycles. Despite tremendous efforts, achieving in situ differentiation and real-time dynamic monitoring of chemoresistant tumor cells from both tumor and normal cells remains a great challenge. Herein, we report, for the first time, a robust adaptive DNA nanoclassifier (RADA) with base excision repair (BER) cascade activity-responsive functionality able to achieve this goal. We demonstrate that the DNA nanoclassifier integrated with four programmable hairpins is capable of adaptively transducing the cascade dynamics of human alkyladenine DNA glycosylase (hAAG) and apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) into a quantifiable fluorescence signal. By taking advantage of its structural programmability, RADA successfully initiates intramolecular catalytic hairpin assembly to generate individual RADA nanoparticles at low hAAG + APE1 expression, which can be transformed into an interconnected network architecture at high hAAG + APE1 expression. This adaptive allosteric process achieves a strong exponential correlation between fluorescence intensity and the logarithm of enzyme concentrations. This finding provides fascinating opportunities for achieving in situ dynamic monitoring of chemoresistance profiling with a range of novel applications in bioimaging and precision medicine.

title: Reprogramming conventional dyes into hypoxia-tolerant type-I photosensitizers via through-space charge-transfer
abstract: Translating ubiquitous conventional fluorescent dyes into hypoxia-tolerant type-I photosensitizers (PSs) is fundamentally bottlenecked by their intrinsically negligible intersystem crossing (ISC) efficiencies, rendering them incompatible with current triplet-dependent design strategies. Herein, we present a universal strategy to reprogram their photophysical pathways via conformation-driven through-space charge transfer (TSCT). Covalently grafting an electron donor onto the dye scaffold via a flexible linker induces spontaneous, non-covalent interaction-driven intramolecular folding in aqueous environments. This constrained donor-acceptor stacking activates a highly efficient singlet charge-transfer state ( 1 CT). The rapid formation of 1 CT minimizes the singlet-triplet energy gap (Δ E ST ), establishing a novel ISC channel that provides an alternative ISC pathway with a significantly reduced energy penalty. The resulting triplet charge-separated state ( 3 CT) efficiently transfers electrons to dissolved oxygen, triggering robust superoxide anion radical (O ·− 2 ) generation. Using Cy5 as a model, we demonstrated that O ·− 2 yield can be precisely modulated solely by tuning the electron-donating capacity. Extending this strategy to rhodamine and coumarin scaffolds unambiguously validates its broad universality. This work provides a versatile blueprint for upgrading commercial fluorophores into high-performance, hypoxia-tolerant photodynamic agents.

title: Asymmetric atomic sites for C2+ production in CO2 electroreduction
abstract: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) to value-added multicarbon (C 2+ ) products plays an important role in artificial carbon cycling and energy sustainability. While single-atom catalysts (SACs) exhibit immense potential due to their ultimate atomic utilization with highly symmetric first coordination spheres ( e.g. , planar M-N 4 moieties) impose severe thermodynamic constraints. This spatial symmetry inherently dictates rigid linear scaling relations (LSRs) among the binding energies of key carbonaceous intermediates and induces strong dipole-dipole electrostatic repulsion during C–C coupling, constituting a fundamental bottleneck for selective C 2+ synthesis. This review systematically encapsulates the emerging frontier of engineering asymmetric active sites via symmetry-breaking strategies to drive efficient C 2+ conversion. Structural tailoring is comprehensively discussed from the perspectives of geometric topological distortion and asymmetric electronic distribution, encompassing first-shell heteroatom doping, axial coordination, in-plane defect engineering, and heteronuclear dual-atom centers. The role of asymmetric coordination in decoupling intermediate binding energies is elucidated through modulating d -band centers, reconstruction of orbital hybridization, and induction of local polarization fields. Such design redirects the reaction pathway from thermodynamically hindered symmetric *CO-*CO dimerization to kinetically favored asymmetric cross-coupling ( e.g. , *CO-*CHO). In addition, the regulation of interfacial hydrophobicity and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) dynamics by asymmetric microenvironment is summarized, revealing the deep-seated mechanisms for suppressing competitive side-reactions. Finally, a forward-looking perspective is presented on overcoming current limitations through advanced in situ spectroscopy, explicit-solvent ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and catalytic stability under industrial-level current densities. This review provides theoretical insights and design principles for engineering asymmetric atomic active sites to break thermodynamic scaling relationships and enable well-defined C–C coupling pathways toward multicarbon products in electrochemical CO 2 RR.

title: An NIR-II AIE photothermal hydrogel with nitric oxide release for synergistic theranostics of refractory fungal wound infections
abstract: Inadequately managed wounds are highly susceptible to microbial colonization, with fungal infections representing a significant clinical challenge due to the biological similarity between fungal and mammalian cells and the adaptive resilience of fungi in hostile environments. Particularly, refractory fungi that respond poorly to conventional anti-fungal therapy or are prone to relapse are the most challenging issue. To overcome these limitations, we have engineered an intelligent thermosensitive dressing by co-encapsulating a second near-infrared (NIR-II) aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photothermal agent (TTBA) and a thermally responsive nitric oxide (NO) prodrug ( S -nitroso- N -acetylpenicillamine, SNAP) within an agarose (AG) hydrogel matrix. This multifunctional system serves not only as a protective physical barrier but also as a theranostic platform capable of modulating the wound microenvironment. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, the photothermal effect of TTBA triggers both localized hyperthermia for anti-fungal photothermal therapy (PTT) and controlled release of NO from SNAP. The released NO further augments therapy by exerting direct anti-fungal activity and mitigating excessive inflammation. Importantly, the thermosensitive hydrogel confines the therapeutic agents to the wound site, enabling precise spatiotemporal delivery while minimizing off-target effects. In vivo studies using a refractory fungal-infected wound model demonstrated accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammatory response, and excellent biocompatibility. Collectively, this photothermally responsive platform offers a targeted, efficient, and adaptive strategy for treating complex fungal wound infections, showing strong clinical potential.

title: Cr-triggered reconstruction coupled with S-anions optimizes mixed-valence metal oxyhydroxide for industrial water electrolysis
abstract: The sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) limits water electrolysis for hydrogen production, calling for robust non-precious metal electrocatalysts. We report a one-step hydrothermal strategy that achieves in situ topological pre-reconstruction of NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH) through the co-introduction of Cr 3+ and S 2− . This drives a bulk phase transformation from LDH to metal oxyhydroxide, overcoming the inherent inertness of LDH. Cr 3+ substitution at Ni sites triggers intralayer rearrangement to form a mixed-valence Ni(Fe,Cr)OOH (NOH) active phase, while S 2− replaces interlayer/in-plane OH − , synergistically tuning the oxidation states of Ni and Fe, enhancing metal–oxygen covalency, and boosting oxygen vacancies. The resulting self-supported S-NiFeCr-NOH/NF electrode exhibits outstanding trifunctional electrocatalytic performance, with overpotentials of only 270 mV (OER) and 321 mV (HER) and a remarkably low overpotential of 193 mV for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR), all at 100 mA cm −2 in alkaline media. A two-electrode cell using S-NiFeCr-NOH/NF as both the anode and cathode requires only 1.95 V to deliver 200 mA cm −2 in the OER ∥ HER configuration. More impressively, when integrated into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), the system achieves a current density of 1500 mA cm −2 at 2.61 V and maintains stable operation for over 150 h. This work, through atomic-scale synergistic doping and synthesis-stage phase engineering, establishes a new paradigm for designing industrial-grade non-precious metal electrocatalysts for water electrolysis.

title: Three-dimensional steric-protected copper clusters for ligand-mediated photothermal conversion and solvent-free click photocatalysis
abstract: Atomically precise copper clusters offer unique opportunities to combine tunable structural, photophysical, and catalytic properties at the molecular level. Herein, we report two copper clusters, [Cu 14 S 2 (L DTC ) 12 ](PPh 4 ) 2 ( Cu 14 , where L DTC = o -dithiocarboxy- o -carborane) and [Cu 8 (L DTC ) 5 (L AT ) 4 ]PPh 4 ( Cu 8 , where L AT = adamantanethiolate), synthesized through a three-dimensional steric ligand-regulation strategy that modulates the core geometry and coordination environment by combining Cu–S coordination with spatial shielding from bulky ligands. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that the Cu 14 cluster, protected solely by L DTC ligands, features a twisted and fully encapsulated Cu 14 S 2 core. In contrast, the Cu 8 cluster presents a hollow Cu 8 S 4 cage hybridized with ligands. This indicates that the metal-ligand interactions lead to completely distinct core structures. Both clusters exhibit exceptional photothermal conversion, with Cu 8 achieving higher initial temperatures, while Cu 14 displays superior cycling stability. Based on their structural and electronic properties, the two clusters exhibit high catalytic efficiency in solvent-free azide-alkyne cycloaddition reactions, with cluster-based turnover numbers (TON) reaching up to 6040 and turnover frequencies (TOF) up to 3020 h −1 . Moreover, they achieve exclusive regioselectivity and demonstrate scalability to the gram scale. This work demonstrates that ligand-tuned copper clusters can serve as multifunctional platforms for integrated photothermal and catalytic applications, providing a molecular-level strategy for sustainable and efficient nanocatalysis.

title: π-conjugated organic cathode enabling Zn2+/H+ co-insertion for ultra-stable aqueous zinc organic batteries
abstract: Organic electrode materials featuring multi-redox sites are highly promising for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), yet their practical application is hindered by high solubility in electrolytes, structural instability under deep reduction, and ambiguous cation-storage mechanisms. Herein, a novel π -conjugated organic molecule, benzo[i]benzo[6,7]quinoxalino[2,3-a]quinoxalino [2,3-c]phenazine-5,14,19,22-tetraone (BQPT), is rationally designed and proposed as a cathode material for AZIBs. The extended π -system of BQPT not only enhances intermolecular π - π stacking interactions, thereby suppressing solubility in aqueous electrolytes, but also endows multiple redox-active sites for high specific capacity. In-situ/ex situ characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal a Zn 2+ /H + co-insertion mechanism for BQPT electrodes, but suffers rapid capacity decay due to byproduct formation and structural instability arising from excessive proton insertion at low potentials. Within optimizing the voltage window (0.4–1.6 V vs. Zn/Zn 2+ ), the BQPT electrodes exhibit a high specific capacity (341.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 ), excellent rate performance (181.1 mAh g −1 at 40 A g −1 ), and remarkable cycling stability (85% capacity retention following 30000 cycles at 25 A g −1 ). This work offers a molecular-level strategy for stabilizing small-molecule organic cathodes and provides valuable insights into the Zn 2+ /H + co-insertion mechanism in AZIBs, advancing the development of high-performance organic electrode materials for energy storage applications.

title: Electronic structure modulation of azide-bridged An-Ln heterobimetallic complexes
abstract: Although the research on azide-bridged polymetallic complexes has been relatively extensive, reports on the introduction of azide groups as π-donor ligands into heterobimetallic (4f-5f) systems composed of 4f lanthanide and 5f actinide metals remain extremely scarce, and systematic investigation of this area has yet to be established. Herein, we first report the synthesis, structural and spectroscopic characterization of two N − 3 -bridged 4f-5f heterobimetallic complexes L D AnN 3 CeL T ( 3-AnCe ) and L T AnN 3 CeL T ( 3′-AnCe ) [An = Th ( 3-ThCe ), U ( 3-UCe ), L D =Trapen DMPS , L T = Trapen TMS , with Trapen = tris(2-aminobenzyl)amine; DMPS = −Si i PrMe 2 , TMS = −SiMe 3 ]. X-ray crystal diffraction reveals asymmetric μ -N 3 coordination in four complexes, adopting torsional trans-bent geometries. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and relativistic quantum-chemical analyses revealed that the spin density is primarily localized on the cerium center, with partial delocalization onto the N − 3 for 3-AnCe . Systematic computational studies on hypothetical L T AnN 3 CeL T (An = Th–Cm) reveal a redox inversion trend: due to the orbital-energy mismatch between the Ln-4f and An-5f orbitals, the electronic ground state of 3-AnCe consists primarily of a 5f π (An)⋯4f π (Ln) configuration, with less mixing of the 6d π (An)-π*(N 3 )-5d π (Ln) configuration. As the actinide atomic number increases, this change in orbital energies results in the oxidation state alternation and electron distribution from An IV -Ce III (An = Th–U) to An III -Ce IV (An = Np–Cm). This work elucidates the interplay of relativistic effects and electronic distribution in f-block heterometallic systems, offering valuable insights for the rational design of unique 4f-5f heterobimetallic complexes.

title: Robust metal-organic frameworks for durable water adsorption: fundamentals and practice
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as exceptionally promising platforms for water vapor adsorption-relevant applications owing to their tunable pore environments and structural diversity/modularity. However, practical applications require not only high working capacity, but also precise control over adsorption thermodynamics, efficient regeneration, and long-term stability under cyclic operation. In this review, we highlight recent advances in the design of robust MOFs for durable water adsorption, with a focus on Zr(IV)- and Cr(III)-based frameworks featuring strong and inert coordination bonds and well-defined pore architectures. We first discuss the fundamental characteristics of water adsorption isotherms and the mechanisms governing water uptake in confined environments. We then examine how reticular chemistry enables the rational construction of hydrolytically stable frameworks with tailored adsorption behavior. Building on these insights, we survey applications in atmospheric water harvesting, adsorption heat transformation, and indoor humidity control, emphasizing the structure-property relationships that dictate performance. Across these systems, four key design strategies emerge, including modulation of pore polarity, optimization of net topology and pore architecture, node-level chemical modification, and expansion of pore volume through hierarchical structures. We conclude with an outlook on challenges and future endeavors toward practical deployment of robust MOF-based water sorbents.

title: Early noninvasive therapeutic response prediction of cancer immunotherapy using a tumor-associated neutrophil elastase-activatable optical nanoprobe
abstract: Conventional fluorescence probes are still limited by inadequate penetration depth, modest resolution, and poor quantitative capacity for monitoring immune states associated with tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) in vivo , which is important for cancer immunotherapy and therapeutic optimization. Here, we constructed an activatable nanoprobe, denoted as DCNC, for noninvasive detection of neutrophil elastase (NE, a TAN-associated functional biomarker) activity via second near-infrared window (NIR-II) ratiometric fluorescence imaging. DCNC consisted of erbium-doped down-conversion nanoparticles and a NE-responsive specific peptide substrate linked with NIR dye Cy7.5, enabling noninvasive real-time dual-excitation ratiometric imaging (under 808 and 980 nm excitation) with self-calibration capability. In vivo imaging demonstrated that the DCNC ratiometric readout quantitatively reported intratumoral NE activity and was associated with TAN-related immune changes during immunotherapy. In mouse Hepa1-6 tumor models, DCNC achieved early, noninvasive stratification of immune responders before macroscopic tumor-burden changes were detectable and facilitated therapeutic optimization in non-responders. Collectively, DCNC holds promise as a noninvasive, real-time, and quantitative optical imaging tool for dynamic monitoring of immunotherapeutic responses through TAN-associated NE activity, thereby guiding personalized treatment strategies.

title: Machine learning-assisted scale-up continuous-flow synthesis of a metal fluoride nanocrystal library
abstract: Large-scale, reproducible ultra-fast synthesis of high-quality metal fluoride nanocrystals is rather crucial for maximizing their potential in diverse industries such as chemicals, energy, and healthcare. However, for most synthetic methods presented so far, only sub-gram quantities of metal fluoride nanocrystals are produced and related steps are often tedious, time-consuming, and laborious. Herein, we present a machine learning-assisted continuous-flow synthesis platform for ultra-fast preparation of 73 metal fluoride nanocrystals, including 12 binary, 55 ternary, and 6 lanthanide-doped nanocrystals at a high rate approaching 80 mmol h −1 . Taking NaBiF 4 nanocrystals as an example, by leveraging data from the phase diagrams of multinary systems, metal precursor-fluoride source-ethylene glycol as inputs, a quantitatively predictive random forest classifier is established to guide the fine-tuning of phase morphology and luminescence features of metal fluoride nanocrystals. Most of those synthesized nanocrystals in our library are very useful, as supported by evidence of lanthanide-doped NaBiF 4 nanocrystals for imaging-guided radiosensitization and real-time radiation dose monitoring during radiotherapy. This work showcases that the machine learning-assisted continuous-flow platform provides a versatile route for scaling up the production of functional metal fluoride nanocrystals as well as other nanostructures, hopefully offering immense promise in fulfilling their actual applications in, for example, cancer theranostics.

title: Single-atom bridge and asymmetric site engineering in homologous covalent heterojunction for matched electron-proton supply in advanced photocatalytic nitrogen fixation
abstract: S-scheme covalent heterojunction offers a promising platform for photocatalytic nitrogen reduction, but achieving high ammonia yield remains challenging due to mismatched charge separation and proton supply. Herein, we report a Ti single-atom (Ti SA ) surface/interface engineering strategy to construct a Bi 2 S 3 /Ti 0.13 Bi 0.87 OBr (R O-Ti-S ) covalent heterojunction via a homologous derivation. The material features a Ti SA -Bi asymmetric site and a covalently linked O-Ti SA -S single-atom bridge and O-Bi-S interfacial motifs that form dual charge-transport channels. The Ti SA -Bi site polarizes and stretches H 2 O to facilitate proton release, while the O-Ti SA -S bridge enables rapid interfacial electron hopping (interfacial charge-transfer rate constant: from 14.62 × 10 −3 ps −1 increasing to 59.26 × 10 −3 ps −1 ). Together, these effects facilitate the high-throughput co-injection of electrons and protons into activated N 2 , resulting in a proton release rate and NH 3 yield of 783.19 and 246.73 µmol g −1 cat h −1 , respectively. The NH 3 yield is 1.56- and 3.95-fold higher than that of the relatively less surface-bound Ti SA in Bi 2 S 3 /Ti 0.13 Bi 0.87 OBr (6%) and Ti-free Bi 2 S 3 /BiOBr homologous heterojunction counterparts, placing this catalyst among the higher-performing N 2 -fixation photocatalysts. Moreover, the Bi 2 S 3 /Ti 0.13 Bi 0.87 OBr (R O-Ti-S ) homologous heterojunction exhibits excellent durability, retaining 96.3% of its activity after five cycles, which is attributed to the strongly integrated components and atomically intimate covalent heterointerfaces.

title: Improving intrinsic thermal conductivity and suppressing high-frequency dielectric loss in liquid crystal epoxy resins
abstract: With the rapid development of high power-density packaging and high-frequency electronic devices, overcoming the intrinsically low thermal conductivity ( λ ) of epoxy resins while maintaining low dielectric loss (tan δ ) under high-frequency electric fields remains a critical challenge. In this work, from the perspective of molecular structure design, aromatic esters containing rigid benzene rings and polar ester groups were employed as mesogenic units to synthesize three thermotropic liquid crystal epoxy monomers (LCE 1–3 ). Among them, LCE 1 exhibits a nematic phase, while LCE 2 and LCE 3 display smectic phases, with liquid crystal temperature ranges of 73 °C–99 °C, 57 °C–68 °C, and 40 °C–69 °C, respectively. During curing, the liquid crystal ordered structures are preserved to varying extents. Notably, the liquid crystal epoxy resin (LCER 2 ) derived from LCE 2 exhibits a highly ordered long-range layered structure, which provides continuous pathways for phonon transport while effectively restricting molecular chain segment motion and polarization response. As a result, the synergistic optimization of high λ and low tan δ is achieved. The intrinsic λ of LCER 2 achieves 0.37 W/(m K), representing an improvement of approximately 106% compared to that of conventional E-51 resin (0.18 W/(m K)). Meanwhile, at a frequency of 10 GHz, its dielectric constant ( ε ) and tan δ are 2.42 and 0.010, respectively, which are reduced by about 31% and 82% compared with those of E-51 ( ε = 3.50, tan δ = 0.054), demonstrating excellent high-frequency signal transmission stability. This work achieves a synergistic enhancement of λ and reduction of tan δ in epoxy resins, providing a molecular design strategy that combines superior performance with good processability for electronic packaging materials targeting high power-density and high-frequency applications.

title: Nickel-catalyzed radical fluorosulfonyl-alkylation to access structurally diverse sulfonyl fluorides
Stabilizing the high-voltage LMFP cathode interface: an unsaturated sulfonate additive strategy
abstract: Lithium manganese iron phosphate (LiMn x Fe 1− x PO 4 , LMFP) cathodes have emerged as promising candidates for lithium-ion batteries, driven by relatively high operating voltage (∼4.1 V vs. Li + /Li), inherent safety, and cost-effectiveness. However, the poor interfacial compatibility between the LMFP cathode and electrolyte, together with HF-induced interfacial corrosion arising from the hydrolysis of LiPF 6 , accelerates transition-metal dissolution and electrolyte decomposition, greatly affecting the cycling stability. Herein, prop-2-yn-1-yl methanesulfonate (PMS), an unsaturated sulfonate additive, is rationally proposed to address these challenges. Its highly reactive C≡C bond, in conjunction with the sulfonate moiety, promotes the formation of a robust polymeric cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) with low interfacial resistance. Moreover, the electron-rich alkynyl functionality enables efficient scavenging of detrimental HF in the electrolyte. Attributed to these synergistic merits, by incorporating only 1.0 vol.% PMS into the conventional electrolyte, the Gr∥LMFP cell delivers a capacity retention of 81.25% after 750 cycles under a high cutoff voltage of 4.5 V. This work demonstrates a cost-effective and highly efficient multifunctional additive strategy for achieving superior long-term cycling stability in high-voltage LMFP batteries.

title: Electrocatalytic acidic oxygen evolution reaction in water splitting: fundamental understanding of the reaction mechanisms
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), a pivotal technology for green hydrogen production, exhibit constrained efficiency due to the sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Moreover, the poor stability of catalysts in harsh acidic environments poses a significant obstacle to the large-scale deployment. In recent years, researchers have devoted their efforts to the advanced design and interpretation of structure-property relations from a more mechanistic perspective. In view of these breakthroughs, the present review elucidates the catalytic mechanisms, i.e., adsorbate evolution mechanism, lattice oxygen mechanism, and oxide path mechanism, and their differences. Subsequently, the rational strategies for catalyst design were discussed, with particular emphasis placed on structure-activity relationships between covalency, spin-state, and orbital hybridization. Furthermore, the crucial role of molecular and atomic level characterization in analysing the dynamic structural evolution, intermediate adsorption behaviour, and verifying the reaction mechanisms during the OER process was highlighted. Finally, the current urgent challenges and future development directions were reviewed. This review provides a comprehensive reference framework for the design of high-performance acidic OER catalysts and the commercialisation of PEMWEs.

title: Base-activated chlorobis(trifluoromethyl)carbinol ester: a versatile platform for constructing gem-bis(trifluoromethyl) scaffolds
abstract: gem -Bis(trifluoromethyl) scaffolds are crucial structural elements in drug discovery, agrochemistry, and materials science, making their precise installation a key objective in organofluorine synthesis. Here, we present chlorobis(trifluoromethyl)carbinol ester (Cl-BTFCE) as a versatile, bench-stable reagent for constructing a diverse range of high-value gem -bis(trifluoromethyl) frameworks. Upon base activation, Cl-BTFCE acts as a potent bifunctional precursor, enabling the controlled in-situ generation of anhydrous hexafluoroacetone (HFA) and reactive acyl species under mild conditions. This platform enables ten distinct transformations, characterized by a broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance. The utility of this protocol is further demonstrated through the late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceuticals and natural products, providing streamlined access to a variety of gem -bis(trifluoromethyl) architectures that were previously challenging to synthesize.

title: Suppressed exciton thermalization losses in narrow bandgap acceptors enable high-performance perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
Sulfur⋯nitrogen intramolecular noncovalent interactions in high-performance organic semiconductors
Boosting tunable photocatalytic syngas production from CO2 and H2O via synergistic optimization of charge separation and d-band engineering
abstract: Efficient photocatalytic CO 2 reduction is crucial for sustainable energy and carbon neutrality, yet its efficiency enhancement is still constrained by limited charge transfer and weak CO 2 adsorption/activation. Herein, we report a Gd-doped ZnIn 2 S 4 (Gd-ZIS) photocatalyst for CO 2 reduction, which enables regulation of the CO/H 2 ratio in the range of 4:1 to 1:1, with CO and H 2 evolution rates reaching 100.3 and 87.3 µmol g −1 h −1 , respectively. The structure of Gd-ZIS and its catalytic mechanism for CO 2 photoreduction were systematically studied. Density functional theory calculations demonstrated that Gd doping can upshift the d-band center of ZIS. This shift not only reconstructs the electronic structure of ZIS and enhances the surface adsorption and activation of CO 2 to promote CO generation, but also facilitates the directional accumulation of electrons around the Gd active sites. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy proved that Gd-ZIS significantly improves the separation efficiency of photogenerated electron-hole pairs, leading to effectively reduced charge transfer resistance as revealed by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The synergistic coupling between CO 2 adsorption/activation and the enhanced charge transfer effect constructs a high-efficiency catalytic mechanism. This study provides fundamental insights into the rational design of photocatalysts and the underlying mechanisms for controllable syngas synthesis from CO 2 reduction.

title: Thiyl radical-catalyzed skeletal reorganization via SO2-retentive Smiles rearrangement
abstract: Skeletal reorganization offers an ingenious strategy for constructing complex molecular architectures—otherwise challenging to access—with high atom- and step-economy. Herein, we report a novel thiyl radical-catalyzed skeletal reorganization that provides efficient access to valuable cyclic N -acylsulfonamide derivatives. This transformation proceeds through a vinyl cyclopropane ring-opening followed by an unusual SO 2 -retentive radical Smiles rearrangement. Conducted under metal-free conditions, the reaction achieves 100% atom economy and exhibits broad functional group tolerance. This work not only expands the scope of radical catalysis but also introduces a new mode for SO 2 -retentive Smiles rearrangements and radical-mediated skeletal reorganization.

title: Extended conjugated organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors for bioelectronic applications of organic electrochemical transistors
abstract: Developing high-performance organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) is crucial for achieving organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) derived logic circuits and bioelectronics. However, there are still significant challenges in realizing high figure-of-merit ( μ C*), mainly due to the molecular design of OMIECs focusing on enhancing charge mobility ( μ ) by improving molecular planarity and crystallinity, yet this often leads to decreased volumetric capacitance (C*). Herein, we develop three polymers named p(g2T-TT)(5O), p(g2T-TPT), and p(g2T-TTT) to probe the effect of π-spacers (including thieno[3,2- b ]thiophene/TT, benzo [1,2- b :4,5- b ′]dithiophene/TPT, and dithieno[3,2- b :2′3′- d ]thiophene/TTT) with different conjugation length and electron-donating ability on molecular planarity and energy levels. Among them, p(g2T-TTT) with simultaneously enhanced planarity and favorable energy levels offers both superior μ and C* values, leading to an ultra-high μ C* (1687.8 ± 30.9 F cm −1 V −1 s −1 ) with excellent μ (6.80 ± 0.21 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), and its OECTs show superior operational stability and maintain a high current density of 450 A cm −2 (with 85.1% retention of initial current) after 3600 s of continuous cycling. Such p(g2T-TTT)-based OECTs enable the unipolar inverters with record-high gain (224 V V −1 ) and the electrocardiogram monitoring with strong signal amplification, respectively. These results indicate that p(g2T-TTT) is a promising OMIEC for constructing the state-of-the-art OECTs-derived low-voltage logic circuit and bioelectronic applications.

title: Unraveling the formation mechanism of solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries
abstract: Solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is pivotal in determining the stability of lithium (Li) metal batteries. However, a fundamental understanding of the formation mechanism of SEI remains elusive. Here, the formation mechanism of SEI and the effect of the electrolyte solvation structure on the SEI formation process in localized high-concentration electrolytes are elucidated. The SEI formation process includes nucleation and growth stages. As the Li salt concentration in the electrolyte increases, the initially dispersed aggregates progressively coalesce, forming a network of interconnected aggregates. The interconnected aggregates expedite the decomposition of anions, thereby increasing the number of nucleation sites for inorganic nanoparticles on the anode. The concurrent growth of extensive and dense nucleation sites can rapidly envelop and passivate Li metal anodes, thereby facilitating the formation of a thin SEI. Conversely, a thick SEI results from the growth of sporadic nucleation sites for inorganic nanoparticles. The formation of a thin SEI reduces the consumption of active Li and electrolytes, enabling a cycle life of 100 cycles in a 500 Wh kg −1 Li metal pouch cell. This work reveals the formation mechanism of SEI and demonstrates principles for regulating the SEI formation process toward long-cycling Li metal batteries.

title: Insights into the photocatalytic mechanism in a nanopotential well@homojunction system: carrier dynamics of the TiO2/ZnIn2S*4/ZnIn2S4 quantum dot system
abstract: The migration and separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers is the core bottleneck restricting the performance of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. To break through the limitations of facile recombination and disordered migration paths of carriers in traditional photocatalytic materials, this work proposes a novel charge carrier migration mechanism mediated by “nano-potential well-induced bidirectional localization and homojunction-enabled unimpeded interface transport”, which is realized by constructing a TiO 2 /ZIS*/ZIS QDs (T-Z*-Q) ternary synergistic system. Taking advantage of the staggered energy bands of the two materials, the nano-potential well achieves bidirectional trapping and directional localization of photogenerated electrons. Meanwhile, ZIS quantum dots (QDs) were introduced to construct a homojunction with ZIS nanosheets. Benefiting from the inherent lattice-matching advantage of the homojunction, this structure eliminates the interface potential barrier, ensuring the efficient transport of carriers from localized sites to the catalytic surface. Surface photovoltage (SPV) measurement results show that the surface potential of T-Z* with a molecular framework structure is much higher than that of pristine ZIS, indicating that the potential difference formed by the nano-potential well can provide sufficient directional driving force for photogenerated carrier pairs. The proposed novel charge transfer mechanism is further validated by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, including work function, density of states (DOS), and charge density difference, and the results confirm the electron transfer pathway from ZIS to TiO 2 . Photocatalytic performance tests demonstrate that the T-Z*-Q ternary synergistic system exhibits excellent hydrogen evolution activity: the maximum hydrogen evolution rate reaches 65.971 mmol g −1 h −1 in pure water, which is 201.13 times that of ZIS nanosheets and 8246 times that of QDs alone. Even in complex seawater environments, it still maintains a high-efficiency hydrogen production capacity of 30.21 mmol g −1 h −1 with a maximum apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 33.07%. This work provides an innovative strategy for regulating charge carrier migration, offering new insights into the design of high-efficiency and salt-tolerant photocatalytic hydrogen evolution materials.

title: Rational design and controllable fabrication of organic charge-transfer cocrystals for optoelectronic applications
abstract: Organic charge-transfer (CT) cocrystals, as an emerging class of functional materials facilely self-assembled from electronic donors and acceptors, have attracted considerable attention across multiple research disciplines. By leveraging unique molecular packing, tunable CT interactions, and tailored electronic levels, their morphologies and optoelectronic properties could be precisely modulated for diverse functionalities. This review comprehensively summarizes the rational design and controllable preparation of organic CT cocrystals with desired low-dimensional structure and optoelectronic features via fine manipulation of intermolecular interactions, molecular packing modes, and thermodynamics/kinetics of the growth process. Beyond well-established characteristics, involving ambipolar transport, nonlinear optical response, near-infrared detection, solar photoelectronic generators, and stimulus-responsive behaviors, many advanced optoelectronic applications have also been discussed. Impressively, future perspectives and potential research directions for organic CT cocrystals, such as flexible electronics, advanced optical computing, and highly efficient energy harvesting, are outlined to motivate further exploration of their multifunctional capabilities and practical implementations.

title: Polymer-deformation-induced reversible mechanoresponsive luminescent switching for visualized mechanical detection
abstract: Organic mechanoresponsive luminescent (MRL) materials capable of visualizing polymer deformations are highly desirable for structural health monitoring. However, achieving sensitive and reversible luminescent responses to subtle changes in the polymer microenvironment remains a challenge. Herein, we report a unique polymer-network-transformation-induced on-off MRL system for dynamic and real-time polymer deformation visualization. The key molecular design of the MRLgen relies on rational modulation of intersystem-crossing-driven fluorescence switching and the molecular symmetry of nitro-cyano-substituted tetraphenylethylene. The proposed TPE-3N-CN exhibits a turn-on-type MRL behavior characterized by dynamic, sensitive switching between a non-emissive crystalline state and an emissive amorphous state with an ultrahigh fluorescence contrast ratio (>3 × 10 3 ). Importantly, the polyurethane network promotes the spontaneous self-microcrystallization of the embedded TPE-3N-CN under ambient conditions, without requiring any external stimuli ( e.g. , organic solvent or thermal treatment), thereby directly yielding a non-emissive pristine state. Upon deformation, abundant hydrogen-bonding interactions within the TPE-3N-CN@polyurethane facilitate the mechanical stress transfer from the polymer matrix to MRLgen, accompanied by the emergence of bright green fluorescence. Such an on-off polymeric MRLgen with spontaneous reversibility and outstanding sensitivity provides an ideal platform for quantitative strain mapping and in situ microdamage-healing visualization, which is simplified and effective for probing the mechanical behavior of advanced polymeric materials.

title: A dual-anchor self-assembled monolayer with suppressed micellization for high-efficiency large-area organic solar modules
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are pivotal hole-selective layers (HSLs) for high-performance organic photovoltaics (OPVs), yet their scalability is often hampered by non-uniform film formation over large areas. Here, we address this challenge with a synergistic strategy combining molecular design and process engineering. We designed and synthesized a new SAM molecule, indolo[2,3-b] carbazole-5,7-diylbis(4,1-phenylene) bisphosphonic acid (ph-IDCz), featuring dual phosphonic acid anchoring groups on a rigid backbone to promote robust and ordered packing on indium tin oxide (ITO). To mitigate the increased aggregation tendency associated with multi-anchor designs, we further developed a tailored co-solvent system that suppresses solution-phase micellization. This combined approach enables the deposition of highly uniform and defect-minimized monolayers over large areas. As a result, small-area devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.08%. Importantly, this strategy is scalable, with large-area modules (18.20 cm 2 ) achieving a PCE of 16.19%. These results demonstrate that ph-IDCz is an efficient SAM-based HSL for OPVs, highlighting the potential of ultrathin self-assembled interfaces for scalable, high-performance OPV modules.

title: Polymeric materials for inducing immunogenic cell death
abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD), as a pivotal form of cell death that activates the host immune system, holds significant promise in cancer immunotherapy. In recent years, polymeric materials, owing to their tunable properties, biocompatibility, and functional versatility, have emerged as powerful tools for inducing ICD. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying ICD and provides an in-depth discussion of how polymeric materials mediate ICD. Particular emphasis is placed on design strategies for enhancing ICD through polymeric platforms, including tumor microenvironment-responsive materials, photothermal and photodynamic systems, functional polymeric delivery systems, ICD inducer and immunoadjuvant delivery vehicles, novel membrane-disruptive polymers, and multicomponent synergistic systems. These approaches highlight the evolution of polymeric materials from conventional drug delivery vehicles to sophisticated modulators of immune responses. Despite ongoing challenges such as optimizing biocompatibility and improving delivery efficiency, polymer-mediated ICD has demonstrated a transformative shift from responsive drug delivery to precise immunoregulation. Looking forward, future efforts may focus on the rational design of intelligent responsive polymers, the development of multimodal therapeutic systems, and the implementation of personalized strategies. This review aims to provide valuable insights into the design of ICD-inducing polymers and to promote their clinical translation in cancer immunotherapy.

title: Isomeric volatile N-heterocyclic additives enable deterministic crystallization and energy-loss suppression in high-efficiency organic solar cells
abstract: Precise control over crystallization and phase separation remains a fundamental bottleneck for achieving high-performance organic solar cells (OSCs), as excessive energetic disorder and non-radiative energy loss are intrinsically governed by the film-formation-induced molecular organization of the active layer. Herein, two isomeric N-heterocyclic volatile additives, 2,6-dichloropyrazine (PNH-2Cl) and 2,4-dichloropyrimidine (MNH-2Cl), featuring distinct nitrogen positions and electron density distributions, are introduced to regulate the film-formation kinetics of D18:BTP-eC9 blends. Owing to variations in electronic structure stemming from molecular isomerization, the two additives exhibit distinct affinities towards the donor and acceptor materials. Specifically, PNH-2Cl more effectively modulates crystallization kinetics during film formation, which promotes tighter π-π stacking, enhanced molecular ordering, and more favorable donor/acceptor distribution. The optimized morphology facilitates charge generation, transport, and extraction while reducing energetic disorder, leading to a lower Urbach energy and suppressed non-radiative energy loss. As a result, the additive PNH-2Cl enabled layer-by-layer deposited binary devices to achieve a remarkable power conversion efficiency of 20.36% with the non-halogenated solvent. This work demonstrates that isomer-dependent electron density distributions in volatile N-heterocyclic additives provide a deterministic means to regulate crystalline ordering, thereby enhancing charge transport and non-radiative energy loss in high-efficiency OSCs.

title: Unveiling the tandem effect in Cu-based catalysts for urea electrosynthesis
abstract: Renewable energy-driven electrocatalytic C–N coupling using CO 2 and waste NO − 3 offers a sustainable and promising alternative to conventional industrial urea synthesis, simultaneously enabling fertilizer production while mitigating environmental and energy challenges. Despite considerable progress in urea electrosynthesis, current Cu-based catalysts continue to suffer from low current densities and poor urea selectivity, severely limiting practical industrial applications. Recently, tandem catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy to address these limitations. In this review, we systematically highlight recent advances in tandem strategies for Cu-based catalysts toward urea electrosynthesis, focusing on three categories: catalyst tandem, electrolyte-catalyst tandem, and electrochemical-chemical tandem. For each category, we provide in-depth mechanistic insights by combining in-situ characterizations and theoretical calculations. Finally, we discuss key challenges and outline future research directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Geometry matters: refining the concept of “preorganization” for polydentate ligands towards lanthanide coordination
abstract: Ligand preorganization has long been recognized as one of the most effective design principles for lanthanide recognition and discrimination. However, lanthanide ions are both large and highly coordination-demanding, effective ligand design requires not only a preorganized binding cavity but also a close geometric match to the overall coordination polyhedron of the resulting complex. To address this challenge, we report an advanced polydentate ligand design concept that integrates ligand preorganization with geometric adaptability, leading to enhanced overall affinity for lanthanide coordination. By simply altering the conjugation sequence of the pyridine and phenanthroline units in the benchmark ligand of DPP , we developed a new ligand PBPy that outperforms the conventional phenanthroline-bipyridine combination. The asymmetric PBPy framework combines the intrinsic preorganization of the phenanthroline moiety with the conformational flexibility of the bipyridine unit, a feature that proves critical for achieving an optimal geometric match as the ligand adapts from its free state to the coordination architecture required in the complex. Representative lanthanide binding constants together with single-crystal structural analyses strongly support this ligand design concept. Theoretical calculations further reveal that the stronger binding affinity of PBPy originates mainly from its lower structural distortion energy compared with DPP . Taken together, this work refines the prevailing concept of ligand preorganization by emphasizing the importance of geometric matching and thus provides a useful guideline for the future design of high-performance ligands for lanthanide sensing, separation, and extraction as well as for stable f-block pharmaceutical applications.

title: Emerging pathways of light cycle oil upgrading to high-quality fuels and petrochemicals
Sulfonation-activated covalent crosslinking of inert asphalt for molecularly tailored hard carbons
Weakly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water promotes C–C coupling by regulating *H supply in CO2 electroreduction
Recent progress in syntheses of silica-based zeolites
abstract: Silica-based zeolites are indispensable in fields of catalysis and adsorption-separation, but their diversity, including structures and compositions, is still greatly limited due to narrow synthesis windows and thermodynamic barriers. To solve these problems, a series of synthetic strategies have recently been developed, aimed at expanding the synthesis of silica-based zeolites, including rational design of organic structure-directing agents (OSDAs), charge density mismatch (CDM), excess fluoride approach, reconstruction route, solvent-free synthesis, and near-neutral synthesis. These approaches effectively enable the synthesis of pure-silica, high-silica, and heteroatom-substituted zeolites with enhanced stability and catalytically active sites. Furthermore, this review also suggests challenges and perspectives for the construction and engineering of active centers and synthesis and control of zeolite structure and morphology in the future.

title: Perylene diimide-based heteroleptic hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks with improved electron transfer for highly efficient visible-light-driven photocatalysis
abstract: Constructing crystalline donor—acceptor (D—A) hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) with efficient charge transport remains challenging due to the need to balance complementary molecular geometry, robust hydrogen-bonding motifs, and long-range supramolecular packing. Herein, we report a heteroleptic strategy that integrates electron-rich tetrapyridyl tetraphenylethylene ( TPTPE ) or tetrapyridyl dibenz[g,p]chrysene ( TPDBC ) donors with an electron-deficient tetracarboxylic perylene diimide (PDI) acceptor to construct two D—A HOFs, HOF-PDI-TPE and HOF-PDI-DBC . Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals ordered alternate stacking of donors and acceptors, with HOF-PDI-DBC showing the strongest π — π stacking and most favourable charge-transfer pathways, leading to narrowed bandgap, enhanced reactive oxygen species generation, and suppressed charge recombination. Consequently, HOF-PDI-DBC enables the green-light-driven photocatalytic condensation of o -phenylenediamine with aromatic aldehydes, delivering benzimidazoles with near-quantitative conversions and up to 90% isolated yields within 2.5 h. Spectroscopic and computational studies confirm that both 1 O 2 and O •− 2 mediate the oxidative cyclization via synergistic energy- and electron-transfer pathways. This work demonstrates a generalizable heteroleptic design principle for engineering electronically coupled HOFs and highlights the potential of ordered D—A frameworks in photocatalysis.

title: The Cu electrode derived from the electro-reduction of Cu-EDTA pollutants for the electrocatalytic conversion of nitrate
abstract: Electrocatalytic reduction of copper ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (Cu-EDTA), a refractory heavy-metal complex pollutant, represents an important approach for both wastewater treatment and efficient recovery of metallic copper. Meanwhile, Cu-based catalysts have exhibited exceptional performance in the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO − 3 RR) to NH 3 . These advances imply that the copper ions present in waste etchant could serve as a suitable metal source for constructing high-performance electrocatalysts to convert nitrate into valuable ammonia, thereby materializing the paradigm of waste valorization. However, the selective reduction of Cu from the Cu-EDTA complex suffers from high overpotential and low Faradaic efficiency (FE). Herein, we achieved up to 83% FE and ~90% copper recovery rate within 10 min from Cu-EDTA using nickel foam (NF) as a cathode at −0.28 V. Simultaneously, a uniform copper-loaded NF (Cu/NF) electrode was fabricated during the Cu 2+ electrodeposition process owing to the regulatory effect of the EDTA ligand. Subsequently, the as-obtained Cu/NF was further used for electrocatalytic NO − 3 RR, which exhibited a high ammonia production rate of >4 mg h −1 cm −2 with a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 70% at −0.4 V. This study offers a viable strategy for the treatment and resource recovery of heavy-metal complex pollutants, with potential applications in wastewater remediation and metal recycling.

title: Chiral co-assembly enables efficient white circularly polarized electroluminescence from monosubstituted helical polyacetylene
abstract: Helical polymers with circularly polarized luminescence have attracted rapidly growing interest; however, achieving circularly polarized electroluminescence (CPEL) from such materials remains a significant challenge. Herein, an achiral monosubstituted polyacetylene (PBPA) featuring a donor-acceptor electronic structure is synthesized. Through a chiral co-assembly strategy using chiral poly(9,9-dioctylfluorene) (PFO) as the host and the as-prepared PBPA as the guest, efficient circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CP-OLEDs) are constructed. Notably, PBPA not only modulates the emission color of CPEL but also acts as a chirality amplifier, effectively enhancing the electroluminescence dissymmetry factor ( g EL ). At a PBPA doping ratio of 3%, the blue emission from the PFO host and the yellow emission from the PBPA guest are precisely balanced, yielding white CP-OLEDs with a high | g EL | of 0.26 and a maximum brightness of 10521 cd m −2 . This study offers new insights into the design of helical polymers for high-performance circularly polarized optoelectronic devices.

title: Interface-controlled bulk spillover in heterogeneous catalysis
Reconciling high ionic liquid loading with high mechanical strength in self-healing ionogels via MOF-polymer coordination
abstract: High ionic liquid (IL) loading (>80 wt%) in self-healing ionogels typically leads to severe mechanical deterioration, thereby limiting their practical applications. Herein, a metal-organic framework (MOF)-polymer coordination strategy is proposed to address this trade-off. By incorporating ZIF-8 nanoparticles (NPs) into carbonyl-rich self-healing polyurethane (CSPU) loaded with 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide, self-healing ionogels with an IL content of 80 wt% are fabricated. Robust coordination bonds formed between unsaturated Zn 2+ ions on ZIF-8 NPs and carbonyl groups in CSPU endow the ionogels with a record-high tensile stress of 5.45 MPa (1.62× higher than that of state-of-the-art self-healing ionogels with comparable IL content), along with exceptional puncture resistance and impact resilience. Simultaneously, the reversibility of these coordination bonds, combined with multiple hydrogen-bonding interactions in CSPU, affords a remarkable healing efficiency of 99.1%. In contrast, SiO 2 NP-reinforced control ionogels exhibit only 68.4% and 76.3% of the tensile stress and healing efficiency, respectively, compared to those of ZIF-8-reinforced ionogels, thereby validating the superiority of MOF-polymer coordination over conventional physical entanglement. Furthermore, the intrinsic molecular sieving effect of ZIF-8 NPs imparts outstanding CO 2 separation performance to the ionogels, which can be fully restored after repeated self-healing cycles.

title: An NIR-II-excited biodegradable photothermal agent with record-high photothermal conversion efficiency for tumor phototheranostics
abstract: Photothermal therapy (PTT) is an emerging non-invasive cancer treatment method with multiple advantages, including precise spatiotemporal control, high specificity, and minimal normal tissue damage, etc. , but usually hampered by limited light penetration depth and side effects from residual photothermal agents (PTA) caused by slow elimination. Herein, taking advantage of intramolecular charge transfer and easily oxidizable unsaturated bonds, NNS-TCF is developed to address the aforementioned bottleneck issues. Once formed as nanoparticles (NPs) in aqueous solution, it shows strong absorption beyond 1000 nm, making sure it can be excited by a near-infrared-II laser for higher penetration depth. NNS-TCF NPs can be gradually biodegraded within 5 h after administration, ensuring biosafety. More importantly, its photothermal conversion efficiency is evaluated as up to 82.1%, which is the record value in the reported degradable PTAs, resulting in an impressive tumor inhibition rate of 99.3% in a mouse model.

title: Surface coordination polymer on NiCo-LDH enables rapid M-OOH formation and efficient methanol electrooxidation
abstract: The electrochemical dehydrogenation of lattice hydroxyl groups is a key step in generating high-valent metal active sites for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR). However, this oxidation process may cause structural collapse and reduce the stability of MOR catalysts. We constructed a NiCo-LDH with a surface-confined NiCo-BTB coordination polymer to stabilize the surface structure reconstruction for efficient and stable MOR catalysis. The NiCo-BTB coordination polymer facilitates the dehydrogenation of lattice hydroxyls (M 2+ -O-H ⇌ M 3+ -O), promoting rapid formation of high-valent Ni/Co species, enabling electrochemical reconstruction into the true active phase M-OOH, and stabilizing the surface structure. Furthermore, the surface-confined coordination polymer structure enhances OH − adsorption at the catalyst surface, accelerating the conversion of CHO intermediates to HCOO − . As a result, the optimized NiCo-LDH/BTB achieves a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 90% at 100 mA cm −2 with more than 100 h stability. This work demonstrates that constructing surface-confined coordination polymers provides a promising strategy for designing high-performance transition metal-based electrocatalysts for selective methanol oxidation.

title: Light-driven ethane selective oxidation to C2 liquids
O p-band center engineering in layered double hydroxides for synergistic dynamic adsorption and fast diffusion of NH+4
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have emerged as promising host materials for aqueous ammonium-ion storage. However, overcoming the kinetic bottleneck caused by excessively strong ion coordination to balance dynamic adsorption and rapid diffusion remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we identify the O p-band center ( ɛ p ) as a key descriptor to resolve this dilemma, employing a Zn 2+ /MoO 2- 4 co-modified NiCo-LDH as an ideal verification model. Integrated theoretical and experimental analyses reveal that Zn 2+ incorporation downshifts the O ɛ p to suppress overly strong interfacial binding, unlocking abundant active sites for charge storage. Subsequently, MoO 2- 4 anchoring fine-tunes the ɛ p to an intermediate level, establishing an optimal thermodynamic balance to accelerate dynamic NH + 4 adsorption/desorption. Furthermore, this ɛ p -modulated electronic environment significantly alleviates electrostatic repulsion at hydrogen-terminated sites. Coupled with additional MoO 2- 4 bridging sites, it enables rapid carrier migration via a low-barrier dual-site cooperative diffusion mechanism. Accordingly, the optimized electrode delivers an outstanding reversible capacity of 197 mAh g -1 at 1 A g -1 and sustains 120 mAh g -1 at a high rate of 10 A g -1 , alongside remarkable cycling stability. This study confirms the O ɛ p as a crucial bridge linking microscopic electronic structures to macroscopic storage performance, guiding the rational design of high-efficiency NH + 4 host materials.

title: Free-standing hierarchical porous carbon composite electrode decorated with ultra-small CuO nanoparticles for high-performance zinc-iodine micro-batteries
abstract: Zinc-iodine micro-batteries (ZIMBs) are considered highly promising energy storage micro-devices owing to their remarkable performance, favorable environmental compatibility, and relatively low cost. Nevertheless, conventional ZIMBs encounter issues such as the accumulation and aggregation of electrode materials, the absence of iodine-philic sites, and sluggish reaction kinetics. Hence, utilizing waste wood-derived carbon (WDC) as the substrate, a three-dimensional hierarchical porous carbon independent electrode material anchored by ultrafine copper oxide nanoparticles (3D CuO@AHPC) was fabricated via alkaline etching and salt template-assisted impregnation. 3D WDC offers strong structural support on account of its excellent structural stability. Simultaneously, the incorporation of hierarchical 3D carbon nanoskeletons and CuO nanoparticles into its pores not only elevates the micropore/mesopore ratio of the cathode and strengthens the physical confinement of polyiodides but also optimizes the electronic structure of ultrafine CuO through the d-π conjugation interaction between CuO and hierarchical porous carbon, thereby providing a plethora of iodine adsorption sites. The “adsorption-diffusion-conversion” synergistic catalysis has been accomplished. At a high rate of 50 C, the assembled ZIMBs still retain a specific capacity of 72.25 mAh g −1 , and the capacity retention rate reached 84% after 10,000 cycles, indicating its superior rate performance and ultra-long cycling stability.

title: Sub-nano TiO2 crystal domains embedded in carbon nanospheres reveal fast ion diffusion toward high-rate sodium storage
Built-in electric field-modulated surface reconstruction of Co(OH)2-CeO2 heterostructure on carbonized delignified wood freestanding electrode for robust water oxidation
abstract: Transition cobalt hydroxides are cost-effective oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, yet their low electronic conductivity and insufficient intrinsic activity remain bottlenecks, while conventional conductive substrates suffer from a lack of eco-friendly and rationally designed porous architectures. Herein, we fabricate a freestanding heterostructured Co(OH) 2 -CeO 2 hybrid with a built-in electric field (BIEF) through anion insertion-enhanced electrodeposition on carbonized delignified wood (CDW). Delignified wood preserves the porous channels with enlarged pore size and enhanced specific surface area, optimizing mass transport. Crucially, the Co(OH) 2 -CeO 2 interface generates a robust BIEF, inducing electron depletion in Co(OH) 2 and elevating the cobalt valence state. This BIEF dynamically accelerates the surface reconstruction into highly active CoOOH species at exceptionally low potentials. Theoretical calculations further reveal that this phase evolution shifts the rate-determining step, optimizing oxygen intermediate adsorption and lowering the energy barrier.
