Resultantly, the optimized Co(OH) 2 -CeO 2 @CDW 1200 exhibits performance metrics of η 10 = 238 mV (at 10 mA cm -2 ) and η 100 = 319 mV (at 100 mA cm -2 ), outperforming the commercial RuO 2 . Furthermore, it enables a 1.56 V cell voltage in a two-electrode Co(OH) 2 -CeO 2 ∥Pt/C system, and achieves an industrial current density of 1 A cm -2 at 1.79 V (80 °C) in anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzers while demonstrating robust operational stability for 240 h at 500 mA cm -2 . This work provides a novel strategy integrating biomass-derived substrates with BIEF engineering for practical water electrolysis.

title: Direct radical fluorosulfonylation of (hetero)arenes
abstract: Owing to their appealing properties and versatile reactivity, sulfonyl fluorides have attracted considerable attention across numerous fields, with aromatic sulfonyl fluorides playing a pivotal role in chemical biology and molecular pharmacology. The introduction of -SO 2 F groups via direct C-H fluorosulfonylation of arenes, circumventing the need for prefunctionalization, represents an effective and concise approach for the synthesis of aromatic sulfonyl fluorides; however, this radical variant has remained an unsolved challenge. Herein, we report the first example of a direct radical fluorosulfonylation of aromatics with fluorosulfonyl radicals, enabled by a benzimidazolium-type radical precursor and an iridium photocatalyst under photoredox catalytic conditions. This reaction provides a new and straightforward method for synthesizing a range of aryl and heteroaryl sulfonyl fluorides from readily available arenes and heteroarenes. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and detailed mechanistic studies were performed to afford deeper insight into the reaction mechanism, and the superiority of introducing -SO 2 F groups for diversity synthesis is demonstrated through further transformation via sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click reactions and drug molecule ligation.

title: High-performance self-healable materials through hydrogen-bond cross-linking: from chemical structure design to multifunctional coatings
abstract: Polymer coatings serve as the primary physical barrier for substrates, playing an indispensable role in modern industries such as aerospace, marine engineering, transportation, and advanced manufacturing. However, these coatings are highly susceptible to micro-damage during long-term service. Endowing them with self-healing capabilities is a crucial strategy to extend material lifespan and improve service reliability. However, traditional extrinsic healing systems often disrupt the coating’s microstructure, while intrinsic dynamic covalent systems typically require harsh triggering conditions. In contrast, hydrogen-bond cross-linked supramolecular systems exhibit significant inherent advantages for developing high-performance smart coatings. These systems enable efficient dynamic recombination under mild conditions and provide strong non-covalent interfacial anchoring effects. This review systematically summarizes the molecular design strategies and cutting-edge applications of hydrogen-bonded self-healing materials. We thoroughly discuss internal cross-linking systems based on the self-association of polymer segments, including 2-ureido-4-pyrimidinone (UPy) units, multiple hydrogen-bond arrays, and hydrogen-bond clusters. Furthermore, we examine external cross-linking strategies that rely on functionalized small molecules or nanoparticles. We highlight how researchers overcome the intrinsic trade-off among mechanical strength, extreme toughness, and dynamic healing efficiency. Key approaches analyzed include micro-topological regulation, rigid-flexible phase separation, and hierarchical biomimetic interface engineering. Additionally, we comprehensively elaborate on the core mechanisms and innovative strategies of these supramolecular systems in various advanced applications. These encompass long-lasting anti-corrosion coatings, impact-resistant protection systems, smart marine anti-fouling coatings, and efficient flame-retardant scenarios. Finally, we objectively identify the core bottlenecks in the current field, particularly the sensitivity to complex aqueous media and the persistent strength-healing dilemma. We also provide forward-looking perspectives on the rational design and engineering translation of next-generation, all-weather, smart adaptive protective coatings.

title: Mimicking frustrated Lewis pair active sites on metal N-heterocyclic carbenes promotes N–H activation for propellant burning rate enhancement
abstract: The burning rate of propellant determines rocket motor impulse efficiency, and this, in turn, is predominantly governed by the combustion characteristics of oxidizers. However, the thermal decomposition of the most common oxidizer, ammonium perchlorate (AP), suffers from high-temperature and spatially discrete combustion issues, resulting in limited stability during the propulsion process. We address this at the atomic level by designing a catalytic promoter with a mimicking frustrated Lewis pairs (FLP) motif. Supported by experimental and computational evidence, the Ag–N mimicking FLP sites in silver N-heterocyclic carbene (Ag(I)-NHC) complexes thermodynamically facilitate N–H bond cleavage, accelerating AP’s thermal decomposition. This dual-site, synergistic activation shifts AP degradation to lower temperatures and collapses the conventional two-stage redox process into a rapid, single-step energy release. A representative complex, Ag(I)-NHC-ClO 4 , lowers AP’s main decomposition onset from 416.1 to 274.2 °C and raises the measured energy release from 606 to 1488 J g −1 , surpassing the state-of-the-art catocene and most reported promoters. To demonstrate its applicability, Ag(I)-NHC-ClO 4 -based propellants were fabricated, achieving a high burning rate of 6.08 mm s −1 at 2.5 MPa with maintained low-pressure sensitivity, which outperforms the majority of reported modifiers. The combination of high-activity and dual-site synergy of Ag(I)-NHC complexes ensures operational safety and engine efficiency of propulsion systems.

title: Marangoni-spread oriented membranes with sub-nanoconfined channels for ultrafast ion permeation
abstract: Ion separation is pivotal for sustainable resource recovery and environmental remediation, yet current materials suffer from a critical trade-off between permeability and selectivity. Most display ionic permeability below 1 mol m −2 h −1 , while nanofluidic devices with high permeability are hindered by complex fabrication and poor scalability. Herein, we report a novel “Marangoni-spread oriented” membrane fabricated via a facile Marangoni spreading assembly (MSA) method, where Marangoni flow-induced interfacial shear forces drive the preferential orientation of crown ether (CE) side chains, forming continuous sub-nanochannels. This unique architecture endows the membrane with ultrahigh monovalent ion permeability and exceptional cation selectivity, which is tightly correlated with the intrinsic properties of grafted CEs. Specifically, a membrane achieves an ultrahigh Li + permeation rate of 11.6 mol m −2 h −1 with a Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity ratio of 32 under a concentration gradient in mixed salt solutions, 15-fold higher than commercial Nafion 212, exceeding the current upper bound of permeability of state-of-the-art membranes. DFT calculations reveal that the performance stems from the balanced ion dehydration and CE binding energy. The rapid, scalable MSA method and mechanistic insights provide a new paradigm for designing high-performance ion separation membranes, with promising applications in lithium recovery and wastewater treatment.

title: Stretchable and flame-retardant organic long-persistent luminescent ionogels for life-saving communication
abstract: The failure of stretchable optical materials under extreme conditions, such as fire, poses a serious threat to human safety during disaster response. However, conventional systems cannot ensure reliable optical communication in life-threatening scenarios like smoke-filled environments. Here, we present a class of novel organic long-persistent luminescent (OLPL) ionogels designed to bridge this gap. By synergistically integrating amino-aromatic luminophores and a rigid hydroxypropyl methylcellulose scaffold into a conductive network, we achieve a material platform with exceptional resilience. These ionogels exhibit ultrastretchability (>1900% strain) alongside robust tolerance to water, open flames, and temperatures up to 120 °C. We leverage these properties to demonstrate a highly durable stretchable display and, critically, a real-time optical communication system capable of transmitting information through dense smoke. This work establishes a versatile material strategy for next-generation safety technologies where conventional alternatives are compromised.

title: Proton-controlled structural disorder in NASICON cathodes for sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Structural disorder is often invoked to explain enhanced ion transport in battery materials, yet in most cases it arises incidentally during synthesis and remains difficult to control. In this work, we show that proton activity during sol-gel processing provides an effective chemical handle to regulate the degree of frozen disorder in sodium super ionic conductor (NASICON)-type cathodes, using Na 4 MnV(PO 4 ) 3 (NVMP) as a representative system. Rather than entering the final lattice, protons are proposed to modulate the relative competition among metal-ligand chelation, hydrolysis, polymerization, and esterification during precursor formation, thereby shaping local structural flexibility prior to crystallization while preserving the integrity of the long-range framework. As a result, an intermediate disorder regime is obtained, which is associated with faster Na + transport without introducing excessive electronic defects or structural instability. Cathodes prepared under these conditions exhibit improved rate capability and stable long-term cycling, retaining 85.6% of their capacity at 5 C after 500 cycles. These results highlight the importance of reaction-pathway control in regulating disorder and suggest a potentially general route for balancing ion mobility and structural stability in polyanionic sodium-ion battery cathodes.

title: Brønsted-dominated dual-acid synergy enables efficient room-temperature biomass acetalization over fibrous mesochanneled aluminosilicates
abstract: Acetalization of biomass-derived aldehydes and ketones catalyzed by solid acids represents a promising strategy for producing sustained-release fragrance carriers. Nevertheless, conventional microporous zeolites are plagued by mass transfer constraints and undesired side-reactions, particularly with bulky substrates. Adding to this complexity, the synergistic interplay between coexisting Lewis and Brønsted acid sites remains poorly understood. Here, we design a new-type of protonated fibrous mesochanneled aluminosilicates (H-Fibr-MAS) via in-situ Al incorporation, featuring open mesochannels and balanced Brønsted (Si-OH-Al) and Lewis (non-framework Al) acid sites. H-Fibr-MAS outperforms Al post-loading analogs (AlOx/Fibr-Silica), commercially protonated microporous zeolites and typical acidic metal oxides in biomass acetalization at room temperature (25 °C). Combining structure-activity correlations, site-poisoning experiments, and in-situ difference Fourier transformed infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), we unveil a Brønsted-dominated Lewis-Brønsted acid synergistic mechanism: Lewis acid sites selectively activate the carbonyl group of furfural, while Brønsted acid sites (especially medium-to-strong sites) facilitate the hemiacetal dehydration, the latter step being previously overlooked but exactly decisive in this dual-acid synergy. Our work establishes acid-site engineering and dual-acid synergy as key principles for designing efficient solid acids in biomass valorization.

title: Efficient gas-solid NO-to-NH3 photoreduction over dynamic PtOx/PtO(x−δ) cluster sites with boosted proton-electron coupled transfer
abstract: Under mild continuous-flow gas-solid conditions, the direct conversion of gaseous nitric oxide (NO) in flue gas to pure ammonia (NH 3 ) is hindered by the challenges of sustaining continuous proton-electron coupling and transfer. Here, we develop a PtO x -TiO 2 photocatalyst featuring ultrafine PtO x clusters that sustain continuous electron transfer via dynamic PtO x /PtO ( x−δ ) redox cycling. Upon illumination, PtO x continuously captures photogenerated electrons to form PtO ( x−δ ) and injects them into NO antibonding orbitals, while the PtO x -TiO 2 interface simultaneously drives H 2 O dissociation to provide a steady proton flux. This persistent electron-proton coupling orchestrated by PtO x /PtO ( x−δ ) cluster interface promotes exciton dissociation, interfacial charge separation, and stepwise hydrogenation of NO to NH 3 . Under continuous-flow conditions with 200 ppm NO, PtO x -TiO 2 achieves 76.0% NO conversion, 808.25 mmol m −2 h −1 NH 3 yield, and 98.1% selectivity, representing a 9.1-fold enhancement over pristine TiO 2 and representing the current best performance in the gas-solid phase NO reduction for NH 3 synthesis. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the exceptional activity mainly stems from the facilitated electron-proton coupled transfer via the unique role of PtO x /PtO ( x−δ ) cluster. This work establishes a practical strategy for sustainable NO abatement with green NH 3 production without separation in gas-solid systems.

title: Insights into the effect of carbon materials on CO2 electroreduction: from atomic scale to macroscopic scale
abstract: The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) converts CO 2 into value-added fuels and chemicals. Traditionally, research on carbon-based electrocatalysts has focused primarily on tailoring the intrinsic properties of specific active sites. However, carbon materials are now recognized not merely as inert supports, but as multifunctional platforms that actively participate in electronic modulation, mass transport, and even catalysis itself. Here, we systematically review the control of the catalytic environment via carbon materials, spanning from electronic regulation at the microscopic scale to macroscopic structural design. This ranges from defect engineering and heteroatom doping at the atomic scale, to the stabilization of metal clusters at the nanoscale, and finally to hierarchical pore engineering and gas diffusion electrode design at the micro-macro scale to manage mass transport and stabilize the triple-phase interface. This review proposes a comprehensive design scheme for multi-scale carbon carriers. By leveraging this multi-scale collaborative strategy, the adsorption energy barriers of key intermediates can be precisely adjusted and the local reaction microenvironment optimized, thereby directing the reaction pathway and improving overall efficiency. Ultimately, this work provides valuable insights for the future structural and functional optimization of carbon-based catalysts.

title: A pseudo-four-channel fluorescent probe for dynamic tracking of peroxynitrite fluctuation and its application in visualizing inflammation and acute kidney injury
abstract: Peroxynitrite (ONOO − ) is a critical signaling molecule with a concentration-dependent dual role, yet existing probes struggle to capture its “tipping point” from a physiological messenger to a pathological toxin. To overcome this limitation, we report a pseudo-four-channel fluorescent probe (RS-L) based on a concentration-dependent cascade reaction. At low ONOO − concentrations, the probe’s green (564 nm) and near-infrared (NIR, ∼731 nm) fluorescence channels are synchronously activated, establishing a ratiometric sensing system modulated by Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Conversely, at higher pathological concentrations, an irreversible cleavage of the hemicyanine moiety is triggered, causing a dramatic reconfiguration of the fluorescent output comprising the quenching of the NIR channel, a secondary enhancement of the green fluorescence due to FRET blockage, and the emergence of a new blue channel (∼456 nm). This design generates a multi-parametric output, which can be interpreted as a “pseudo-four-channel” information matrix. This matrix comprises three distinct spectroscopic channels (blue, green, and NIR) and an additional analytical pseudo-channel derived from the ratiometric signal ( I green / I NIR ) for self-calibrated analysis, enabling the intuitive discrimination of ONOO − levels from functional to damaging overload. We have not only clearly visualized the concentration transition of endogenous ONOO − in cellular models of inflammation and acute kidney injury (AKI), but have also successfully extended this tiered monitoring capability to a zebrafish in vivo model. Therefore, RS-L not only provides a promising tool for investigating the concentration-dependent effects of ONOO − but also, its multi-parametric cascade response design paradigm provides a new design paradigm for smart probes capable of decoding complex biological signals.

title: Computationally guided donor-engineering of azahelicenes towards high-performance circularly polarized luminescence
abstract: Developing circularly polarized luminescent (CPL) organic emitters that simultaneously exhibit high emission efficiency and strong chiroptical activity remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a computationally guided design strategy for donor-functionalized azahelicenes with enhanced CPL performance. By evaluating transition dipole moment parameters and predicted g lum values, representative azahelicene candidates were identified, synthesized, and systematically investigated. Single-crystal analysis revealed that donor functionalization and structural locking play crucial roles in modulating helical geometry, molecular rigidity, and intermolecular packing. In solution, these azahelicenes exhibited efficient fluorescence and pronounced chiroptical responses, with ∣ g abs ∣ and ∣ g lum ∣ values reaching the 10 −2 level. Time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations further elucidated the relationship between molecular structure, transition dipole orientation, and CPL activity. Moreover, one azahelicene derivative, AzaICz-1 , displayed reversible pH-responsive luminescence and chiroptical switching, accompanied by red-shifted emission spectra and slightly reduced g values after protonation. This work provides valuable insights into the rational design of high-performance and stimuli-responsive chiral luminescent azahelicenes.

title: Bioorthogonal metabolic-to-DNA hierarchical converter with machine learning decoding reveals cell surface nascent RNA dynamics
abstract: The canonical understanding of RNA biology and chemical biology has been reshaped by recently discovered cell surface RNAs (csRNAs). Critical gaps persist, however, in understanding their dynamic behavior and the spatial relationship between pre-existing and nascent RNA molecules, mainly due to the challenge of differentially interpreting these two csRNA forms with identical sequences. Here we report a live-cell imaging method termed the bioorthogonal metabolic-to-DNA hierarchical converter (BMDHC), designed for nascence-differentiated cell surface spatial transcriptional profiling. It includes both a chemical encoding module and an algorithmic decoding module. Firstly, total csRNAs of interest and their nascent molecules with bioorthogonal labels are each transformed into distinct fluorescence outputs (green and red) by DNA proximity hierarchical encoding. This enables simultaneous spatial mapping of both csRNA forms with the same sequence and assessment of the nascent rate (the ratio of nascent molecules to total ones) in single cells. Secondly, a lightly supervised machine learning algorithm is developed as a decoding analytical pipeline to visualize these high-dimensional image data (green, red, and their ratio). By successfully detecting diverse csRNA classes across different cellular models, we further demonstrate the general applicability of this method. Furthermore, these three-dimensional data of csRNA dynamics were decoded to visualize different cell cycle phases, implying a direct correlation between csRNA synthesis dynamics and fundamental cellular proliferation states.

title: Efficient hydrogen production via electrochemically assisted partial reforming of ethanol on a tandem catalytic electrode
Metal–organic frameworks for multi-component separations: design strategies, mechanisms, and applications
abstract: Separation and purification are crucial in chemical manufacturing for producing valuable chemicals. However, discriminating individual components with similar physicochemical properties in complex mixtures can be challenging. Current practices typically rely on energy-intensive, heat-driven processes such as low-temperature distillation. Adsorptive separation using porous materials represents a promising alternative technology with the potential to reduce energy consumption. Particularly, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have become a class of appealing materials for separation applications, thanks to their tunable pore size and pore chemistry. Nonetheless, the complexity of real feed streams usually exceeds that of lab test samples, as they often contain moisture and other trace impurities. Consequently, separation performance is influenced by the interplay among individual components, and findings such as adsorption capacity and diffusion rates from lab tests on single components or binary mixtures may not adequately reflect the real behavior in practical scenarios. This review highlights recent progress in using MOFs for multi-component separations in gas, vapor, and liquid systems, with a focus on pore engineering and surface engineering as key strategies for optimizing the overall performance in terms of selectivity, diffusion, and working capacity.

title: Preface: special topic on nucleic acid nanotechnology
Boosting photoluminescence yield via bulky substituents in fused ring acceptors enables low-energy-loss organic solar cells
abstract: Non-radiative energy loss (Δ E nr ) is a critical factor limiting the performance of organic solar cells (OSCs), primarily governed by the electroluminescence quantum efficiency ( EQE EL ) of the donor-acceptor charge-transfer (CT) state, which closely correlates with acceptor photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Therefore, enhancing molecular emissive properties while maintaining efficient charge transport is key to overcoming the efficiency bottleneck in OSCs. Here, we introduced a three-dimensional bulky triptycene unit into the fused-ring core of a small-molecule acceptor to explore a new acceptor MZ. The substantial steric hindrance of triptycene effectively suppresses H-type aggregation, leading to significantly enhanced PLQY. The resulting D18:MZ-based device achieves an ultralow Δ E nr of 0.17 eV. Furthermore, incorporating MZ into a high-crystallinity system (D18:L8-BO) enables precise regulation of molecular aggregation behavior and crystallization kinetics, facilitating efficient exciton dissociation. Eventually, the D18:L8-BO:MZ ternary device delivers a remarkable efficiency of 20.61% with a low Δ E nr of 0.18 eV. These findings demonstrate designing acceptor materials with high PLQY represents a rational strategy for further improving the efficiency and minimizing energy loss in OSCs.

title: Anion-π+ driven theranostics: a potent photodynamic strategy against drug-resistant bacterial infections
abstract: Pathogenic bacterial infections, especially those caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, represent a serious threat to public health. The development of efficient antibacterial agents is therefore of great significance. Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogens offer unique advantages for photodynamic antibacterial therapy, yet a generalizable design strategy remains lacking. To address the challenge of drug-resistant bacterial infections, this study constructed a novel molecule, TTPA-MePy, by introducing anion- π + interactions. We aimed to modulate molecular properties through weak interactions and develop an efficient phototheranostic antibacterial material. Quantum chemical calculations, molecular dynamics simulations, and crystal structure analyses revealed that the bright aggregation-induced emission is mainly governed by the twisted molecular conformation and loose intermolecular packing that restricsts π - π stacking, whereas the anion- π + interaction chiefly reshapes the excited-state energy-dissipation pathway through enhanced spin-orbit coupling and a reduced singlet-triplet gap to switch on efficient intersystem crossing and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Experimental results showed that TTPA-MePy nanoparticles (NPs) exhibit a high quantum yield and efficient ROS generation. At the molecular level, the cationic TTPA-MePy binds to negatively charged bacterial surfaces through electrostatic interactions, while the corresponding TTPA-MePy NPs serve as a biocompatible photodynamic platform that, upon white light irradiation, exhibits potent killing activity against both Staphylococcus aureus (SA) and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), as well as strong anti-biofilm capability. In a murine model of MRSA-infected skin wounds, TTPA-MePy NPs combined with white light irradiation achieved a wound healing rate of 99.56%, along with effective bacterial clearance, reduced inflammation, and enhanced tissue regeneration, while showing good biosafety. In summary, this work demonstrates that anion- π + interactions can synergistically optimize the photophysical properties and antibacterial performance of AIEgens. TTPA-MePy NPs integrate efficient photodynamic antibacterial activity, anti-biofilm capability, and excellent biocompatibility, providing a new strategy and a promising candidate for photodynamic therapy against drug-resistant bacterial infections.

title: Binary molecular passivation stabilizes formamidinium cations for efficient and durable inverted perovskite solar cells
abstract: For inverted (p–i–n) perovskite solar cell efficiencies approach fundamental limits, extended operational stability remains a critical challenge. Conventional interfacial passivation using protonated amine salts ( e.g. , PEAI, EDAI 2 ) suffers from intrinsic chemical vulnerability: these organic cations undergo deprotonation under operational stress, generating neutral amines that irreversibly decompose the formamidinium framework via proton extraction. Herein, we report a binary molecular passivation (BMP) strategy synergistically combining ethylenediammonium diiodide (EDAI 2 ) and thiophene–sulfur–ethyl–phthalimide (T-S-Epht) to address both efficiency and stability limitations. T-S-Epht selectively anchors formamidinium cations through interfacial hydrogen bonding, suppressing deprotonation-induced degradation while preserving EDAI 2 defect-passivation function. Density functional theory calculations reveal a synergistic binding energy of −4.01 eV for the co-adsorbed system. This dual management of chemical stability and electronic properties enables a 26.48% power conversion efficiency with a 1.20 V open-circuit voltage. Crucially, the BMP interface maintains stable surface energetics under severe thermal and photostress, confirmed by Kelvin probe force microscopy. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% initial efficiency after 1750 h of continuous 1-sun illumination at maximum power point (ISOS-L-1I) and 97.5% after 1800 h shelf storage. This molecular engineering paradigm establishes a robust pathway toward maximizing efficiency and longevity in perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Leaving group match-up-enabled photocatalytic nucleophilic 18F-deoxyfluorination of highly electron-rich catechol derivatives: facile automated synthesis of [18F]FDOPA for clinical diagnosis
abstract: Abstract The nucleophilic aryl 18 F-fluorination of catechol derivatives has long presented a challenge due to the repulsion of the high electron density aromatic ring against the attack of 18 F-fluoride, which has limited the development and production of PET tracers. Here, we report a photocatalyzed aryl 18 F-deoxyfluorination strategy for the efficient 18 F-labeling of the catechol moiety, facilitating the synthesis of the PET tracer [ 18 F]FDOPA. The challenging direct nucleophilic 18 F-fluorination was ultimately achieved by fine-tuning the electronic properties of the aromatic ring with different O -derived leaving groups to align with the photocatalysis system. Various precursors were rapidly prepared and investigated under azeotropic drying-free photolabeling conditions, with several precursors showing notable potential for the synthesis of [ 18 F]FDOPA. The substrate 3i , which bears a 4,5-dicyano-2-fluorophenoxy leaving group and demonstrates excellent 18 F-deoxyfluorination efficiency, was selected for further optimization towards scale-up synthesis. The [ 18 F]FDOPA was successfully produced in 16.5% - 21.2% (n = 5) non-decay corrected RCY within 80 minutes with 6.45 ± 2.39 Ci/μmol molar activity on a commercial radiosynthesis module using an innovative RFTA photocatalyst. The readily available and stable precursor makes this transition-metal-free approach an attractive routine for the daily production of [ 18 F]FDOPA with high molar activity, which also paves the way for the nucleophilic 18 F-fluorination of other catechol derivatives.

title: High-efficiency pure organic deep-red room-temperature phosphorescent probes: from dissolved oxygen sensing to glucose detection
abstract: Pure organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials often exhibit low efficiency due to intrinsically weak spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which severely limits their practical applications. However, their high sensitivity to environmental stimuli offers unique opportunities for responsive sensing. In this work, based on a functional unit combination strategy, three positional isomers (4,7-2Se, 4,6-2Se, and 4,5-2Se) are synthesized by integrating a benzothiadiazole (benzo[ c ][1,2,5]thiadiazole, BZT) core with two phenylselenyl substituents (Ph–Se). The geometric torsion of the Ph–Se moiety is induced by steric hindrance between them, promoting an orthogonal orientation between the non-bonding (n) orbital of the selenium (Se) atom and the π orbital of the BZT core. This structural feature works in synergy with the heavy-atom effect of selenium, significantly enhancing the SOC. Among the three isomers, 4,5-2Se exhibits efficient deep-red RTP emission. Its water-soluble nanoparticles prepared by polymer encapsulation exhibit excellent oxygen sensitivity, enabling accurate and quantitative detection of dissolved oxygen. On this basis, combined with the oxygen-consuming reaction catalyzed by glucose oxidase (GOx), the glucose concentration can be accurately detected in vitro . Overall, this work provides a novel molecular design strategy for efficient pure organic deep-red RTP and broadens its application prospects in the life sciences for oxygen-related biochemical analyte sensing and detection.

title: A copper-hemiporphyrazine-based 2D conjugated metal-organic framework
A β-alkylidene handle unlocks circularity and tunable performance in polyhydroxyalkanoates
Chlorine-corrosion-resistant high-performance oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysts enabling green seawater electrolysis
abstract: Direct electrolysis of seawater offers a sustainable route for low-cost green hydrogen production. But this solution is severely hindered by Cl − -induced competitive adsorption and anode corrosion issues. Herein, using the industrial by-product SiCl 4 , successfully prepared a spherical “armor”-structured Si-NiFeOOH/NF via a rapid etching technique as an efficient anode catalyst. Si doping optimizes the electronic structure for enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, while the in-situ -formed physical barrier effectively suppresses Cl − corrosion. The electrochemical test results show that in the simulated seawater/seawater, the overpotential of Si-NiFeOOH/NF at 10 and 100 mA cm −2 is only 245 mV/231 mV and 299 mV/307 mV respectively, and it exhibits excellent stability (>160 h at 100 mA cm −2 ). Meanwhile, in the two-electrode freshwater/seawater system, reach 100 mA cm −2 is only 1.76 V/1.84 V, and the durability exceeds 140 h. More importantly, anion exchange membrane water electrolysis system (AEMWE) test results confirmed the practical application feasibility (stable >50 h at 1000 mA cm −2 ). Mechanistic studies reveal that Si doping lowers the rate-determining step (RDS) energy barrier and suppresses Cl − adsorption/corrosion, thereby enhancing both OER activity and chlorine corrosion resistance. This study provides technical support for the anti-corrosion design and scale-up application of OER electrocatalysts in seawater media.

title: The challenges and opportunities of single-atom-site catalysts in industrial applications
Hofmeister-driven cation–anion synergy enables high-power and ultra-stable cryogenic aqueous zinc–iodine batteries
Spatially decoupled heavy-atom and steric engineering enables fast RISC and concentration-insensitive narrowband blue MR-TADF emitters
abstract: Blue multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters combining high exciton utilization and high color purity remain highly desirable yet fundamentally constrained by slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) process and aggregation-induced spectral deterioration. Here, we report a spatially decoupled heavy-atom and steric engineering strategy to simultaneously accelerate RISC and suppress intermolecular interactions in blue MR-TADF systems. Three emitters, SBN-DP, SBN-DPS , and SBN-DPSe , were designed by integrating peripheral bulky substituents with externally located chalcogen atoms. This design effectively enhances spin-orbit coupling without perturbing the intrinsic MR core electronic structure. As a result, selenium-containing SBN-DPSe exhibits a rapid RISC rate of 5.1 × 10 5 s -1 while maintaining photoluminescence quantum yields above 95% at different doping concentrations. Sensitizer-free organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on SBN-DPSe deliver narrowband blue emission at 469 nm with a full width at half maximum of 23 nm, Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage coordinates of (0.124, 0.128), a maximum external quantum efficiency of 37.6%, and a maximum luminance of 33458 cd m -2 , together with mitigated efficiency roll-off. This work demonstrates an effective strategy for reconciling fast exciton dynamics with spectral integrity in MR-TADF emitters.

title: Deciphering interfacial hydrogen atom transfer in electrochemical glycerol oxidation on CoOOH
abstract: Glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) for the production of high-value-added products has emerged as a promising and green strategy for valorizing the surplus byproduct of the biodiesel industry. Among various catalysts, CoOOH has been extensively investigated for electrochemical GOR, where the reaction pathway is generally governed by a lattice oxygen-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (LOM-HAT) process. Herein, by resorting to in situ spectroscopy and electrochemical analyses, we unraveled that there is a second and more dominate mechanism, namely adsorbed oxygen (OH ads )-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (AOM-HAT), which contributes more than 70% of the GOR catalytic current density. Furthermore, we developed a sulfate-assisted strategy to boost reconstruction of the precatalyst into an oxygen-deficient CoOOH, which improves formate productivity from 63.7 to 194.8 μmol h -1 cm -2 via lowering the energy barrier for OH ads formation. The catalyst’s practicality is demonstrated in an anion-exchange membrane flow cell, achieving stable glycerol-to-formate electro-oxidation at 20 A for over 100 h. This work provides fundamental mechanistic insights into both GOR and precatalyst reconstruction, establishing design principles for efficient electrocatalysts toward glycerol valorization.

title: An adaptive Schiff base polymer interphase for lithium metal anodes via dynamic cross-linking and molecular anchoring
abstract: Artificial solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) are widely used to stabilize lithium metal anodes, yet most polymeric interphases behave as static coatings and gradually lose their protective effect when cracks and interfacial voids develop during repeated lithium plating and stripping. Herein, we report an adaptive polymer artificial SEI (named BBT) based on Schiff base chemistry to preserve interfacial contact continuity on lithium metal. The resulting BBT layer combines dynamic cross-linking with strong Li-N coordination, enabling simultaneous crack repair and chemical anchoring to the lithium surface. The reversible imine bonds and hydrogen bonding network afford a tensile strength retention of 84.6%, while the sp 2 -hybridized nitrogen atoms in the Schiff base exhibit a strong adsorption energy of −1.76 eV toward Li (110), allowing the polymer to remain tightly attached during interfacial deformation. This adaptive interface suppresses SEI rupture and regeneration, maintains stable interfacial relaxation behavior, and promotes the formation of Li 3 N/Li 2 S-containing ion-conductive components. Consequently, BBT-protected lithium enables stable Li‖Li cycling for over 1600 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . In high-loading LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 (NCM622) pouch cells, the protected anode retains 81.25% capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C, extending the lifetime by nearly 20 times compared with bare lithium. This work establishes adaptive interfacial contact regulation as an effective design principle for durable lithium metal anodes.

title: Electrochemical in situ transformation for constructing function-oriented amorphous nanocatalysts
abstract: Amorphous nanocatalysts, which lack long-range periodic atomic order, often exhibit diverse local coordination environments, structural distortion, and abundant coordinatively unsaturated sites. These features generate heterogeneous electronic states and diversified reaction microenvironments, endowing amorphous catalysts with distinct advantages in electrocatalytic energy conversion and chemical synthesis. However, the intrinsic long-range disorder and isotropy of amorphous materials also make it difficult to precisely construct regular morphologies, oriented arrays, and hierarchical channels through facet-selective exposure, crystallographic orientation control, or epitaxial matching, as commonly achieved in crystalline materials. This limitation creates challenges in constructing reactant/product transport pathways, continuous conductive frameworks, liquid-philic/gas-phobic interfaces, and robust catalyst-support-current collector coupling structures, thereby hindering the simultaneous optimization of intrinsic reaction kinetics, interfacial charge-transfer kinetics, and mass-transport kinetics in electrocatalysis. Electrochemical in situ transformation provides a feasible strategy to address this contradiction. This approach typically begins with precursors featuring defined morphologies, oriented structures, spatial confinement or interfacial coupling, and induces surface, near-surface or bulk amorphization under electrochemical working conditions through coordination-bond cleavage, ligand removal, anion leaching, valence-state variation, atomic migration and local structural rearrangement. The resulting amorphous active phases can largely inherit the morphology, channels, conductive networks, and interfacial adhesion of the precursors, while simultaneously introducing the high density of active sites and tunable local electronic structures characteristic of amorphous materials. In this review, we focus on electrochemical in situ transformation as a route to function-oriented amorphous nanocatalysts. Within this framework, we summarize representative transformation pathways, including precursor decomposition, atomic migration, electrochemical multicomponent reconstruction, valence-cycling-induced cumulative amorphization, and reaction-environment-induced secondary amorphous reconstruction. We further clarify how these processes introduce amorphous local active features under the structural constraints imposed by precursors, while concurrently optimizing site activity, electron transfer, reactant transport, product release, and working-state stability. Finally, we discuss key challenges in precursor design, transformation-pathway regulation, and identification of working-state structures, aiming to provide guidance for the rational construction of function-oriented amorphous electrocatalysts.

title: Tandem upcycling of polybutadiene rubber to olefins over layered self-pillared zeolites with tailored acidity
abstract: Rubber waste is a carbon-rich but underexploited feedstock. Its cross-linked network and competing cracking pathways, however, impede selective conversion to olefins. Here, we report a tandem fixed-bed process that spatially decouples primary polybutadiene (PB) rubber depolymerization from secondary olefin-forming cracking by employing layered self-pillared (LSP) zeolites with stage-specific acidity. In the first stage, mesoporous LSP-Z230, possessing a low overall acid-site density, converts PB into volatile unsaturated oligomers and short-chain intermediates. These species are then upgraded over 1%P-LSP-Z71 in the second stage, where moderate acidity promotes successive β -scission while suppressing hydrogen transfer and aromatization. Under optimized conditions, this tandem system achieves complete PB conversion within 1 h, delivering a C 2 -C 6 olefin yield of 47.8% and a gas-phase olefin selectivity of 92%. Both catalysts retain high activity over five regeneration cycles and remain effective on compositionally complex commercial rubber wastes. Requiring neither noble metals nor external hydrogen, this flow process offers a robust strategy for steering the deconstruction of cross-linked rubber toward value-added olefins.

title: Multiscale cellulose engineering for advanced sodium-ion batteries: from structural modulation to interfacial optimization
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are regarded as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage due to the abundance and low cost of sodium. However, their practical deployment is still hindered by sluggish Na + kinetics, interfacial instability, and safety concerns. Cellulose, the most abundant natural biopolymer, features hierarchical architecture and chemically tailorable surface functionalities, making it a versatile platform for structural and interfacial engineering in SIBs. This work establishes an updated “multiscale cellulose” framework specifically for SIBs. The roles of cellulose across different scales are systematically elucidated: at the macro scale, modulation of biomass components (cellulose/hemicellulose/lignin) governs the microcrystalline evolution of hard carbon, balancing open-pore adsorption and closed-pore filling to regulate slope/plateau sodium storage behavior and initial coulombic efficiency; at the micro-/nano-scale, cellulose serves as a robust host and structural scaffold for electrodes, electrolytes (liquid, quasi-solid, and solid), and separators, with tunable porosity and high thermal stability enhancing ion transport and suppressing dendrite growth; at the molecular scale, surface-group engineering of cellulose in hard-carbon precursors, binders, separator coatings, and polymer electrolytes is emphasized, where polar functional groups strengthen interfacial adhesion, tailor electrode-electrolyte interphase composition, and construct Na + -preferred transport pathways. Finally, this review summarizes the correlations among multiscale structure, surface chemistry, and electrochemical performance, and proposes forward-looking design principles for future cellulose-based SIBs.

title: Molecular nanocarbon-based charge-transfer complexes as photocatalysts for H2O2 production
Zeolite-confined Fe1Cu2 sites enable tandem CO2 hydrogenation to methanol and dimethyl ether
The barrier role of Zr in Zr-rich CeZrOx for stabilizing supported Pt clusters
abstract: Pt cluster catalysts supported on CeO 2 exhibit high activity in oxidizing air pollutants such as CO and hydrocarbons; however, their susceptibility to disintegration and redispersion leads to rapid deactivation under lean-burn conditions, posing a major challenge. In this study, Pt cluster catalysts derived from Pt single atoms anchored on CeO 2 and serial Zr-doped CeO 2 supports were fabricated by H 2 treatment, and their catalytic performance was evaluated in a cyclic CO oxidation test from room temperature to 500 °C. Unlike Pt cluster catalysts supported on CeO 2 or low-Zr-doped CeO 2 , which suffered significant deactivation, with T 50 increasing by ca. 100 °C, the Zr-rich CeZrO x support, represented by Ce 0.3 Zr 0.7 O x , better retained cluster-like Pt species and markedly suppressed activity loss. Although Pt/C3Z7 showed lower initial CO oxidation activity than Pt/CeO 2 , it exhibited markedly improved activity retention during repeated lean-burn cycling, leading to superior apparent performance after multiple cycles. Further characterizations revealed that the intrinsic property of CeO 2 to form strong Pt–O–Ce linkages with Pt promoted the disintegration of Pt clusters and the surface diffusion of Pt atoms, whereas high-concentration Zr 4+ ions, combined with weak Pt-ZrO 2 interaction, suppressed the reformation of Pt–O–Ce linkages. Thus, Zr-rich CeZrO x regulates the dynamic balance between Pt cluster retention and oxidative redispersion. This work provides mechanistic insight into support-controlled Pt restructuring and offers a practical strategy for designing durable CeO 2 -based noble-metal catalysts for emission control.
